celebrity.title: SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.
celebrity.title_en:
SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.

Now, SBI is India's biggest bank. Its balance sheet crossed ₹66 lakh crore this year. Almost every Indian family has some link to it, a salary account, a home loan, a pension.

In October, SBI put out an ad for six AI and tech roles. There is one opening for "General Manager and Chief AI Officer".

The pay is up to ₹1.6 crore a year. SBI says it depends on experience, current pay and posting.

The other five roles pay well too. Three Deputy General Managers get up to ₹1.2 crore each. Two AI architects get up to ₹90 lakh each.

Now SBI's own chairman, CS Setty drew ₹63.87 lakh in FY25. So the AI chief can earn about 2.5 times the person who runs the bank.

Yet, private banks are a different world. 

HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan was paid ₹12.08 crore in FY25. PSU bank CEOs earn only about 5 to 7% of what private bank CEOs earn.

But SBI able to pay its AI chief more than its chairman, because the role is a contract job. It is a three year term, which SBI can extend by two more years.

Basically, it is the workaround. An AI leader at this level won't come at this budget. So SBI is working around it.

As per the ad, the person will set up control rooms for AI and data products with the business teams. They will track how live AI models perform and what risks they carry. 

They will also run a separate team whose job is to check models independently. They will also train staff to use these tools. The role also covers an enterprise AI platform for generative AI and AI agents.

They need at least 15 years in banking, financial services or IT. And at least 3 years in a senior leadership role in AI, analytics, model oversight or governance.

So a brilliant engineer who built great models alone, but never ran a team, can't apply for this.

Honestly, a three year term is very short for building an AI platform inside a bank this size. SBI should use the two year extension while they build a second line of leaders under the CAIO from day one.

Obviously, a chairman earning less than half of what a new hire under him can earn is not a healthy setup. 

The Finance Ministry should let PSU banks pay market rates for specialist roles through a clear policy, instead of a contract workaround every time.

And if you are a senior data or analytics person who wants a role like this in five years, it rewards people who have led teams, owned model risk and worked with business heads. 

Pure technical depth won't be enough.

celebrity.quote_zh:
SBI 为首席人工智能官提供的 1.6 亿卢比的报价很棒，但这也表明 PSU 银行对技术人才的薪酬是多么的破碎。

现在，SBI 是印度最大的银行。今年其资产负债表超过 660 亿卢比。几乎每个印度家庭都与它有某种联系，工资账户、住房贷款、养老金。

10 月，SBI 发布了一则招聘 6 个人工智能和技术职位的广告。有一个“总经理兼首席人工智能官”的职位空缺。

年薪高达 1600 万卢比。 SBI 表示，这取决于经验、当前薪酬和职位。

其他五个角色的报酬也不错。三名副总经理每人的薪酬最高可达 12 万卢比。两名人工智能架构师每人可获得高达 900 万卢比的奖金。

CS Setty 现任 SBI 董事长，2025 财年收入达 638.7 万卢比。因此，人工智能主管的收入大约是银行经营者的 2.5 倍。

然而，私人银行却是一个不同的世界。

HDFC 银行首席执行官 Sashidhar Jagdishan 在 2025 财年的薪酬为 1.208 亿卢比。 PSU 银行首席执行官的收入仅为私人银行首席执行官的 5% 至 7% 左右。

但 SBI 能够向 AI 主管支付比董事长更高的薪酬，因为该职位是合同制工作。任期三年，SBI 可以再延长两年。

基本上，这是解决方法。这个级别的人工智能领导者不会有这样的预算。因此，SBI 正在解决这个问题。

根据广告，此人将与业务团队一起建立人工智能和数据产品的控制室。他们将跟踪实时人工智能模型的表现以及它们带来的风险。

他们还将管理一个单独的团队，其工作是独立检查模型。他们还将培训员工使用这些工具。该角色还涵盖用于生成人工智能和人工智能代理的企业人工智能平台。

他们需要在银行、金融服务或 IT 行业工作至少 15 年。并在人工智能、分析、模型监督或治理领域担任高级领导职务至少 3 年。

因此，一位才华横溢的工程师独自构建了出色的模型，但从未管理过团队，因此无法申请此职位。

老实说，对于在这种规模的银行内部构建人工智能平台来说，三年的期限非常短。 SBI 应该利用两年的延期，从第一天起就在 CAIO 下建立第二线领导人。

显然，董事长的收入还不到他手下新员工收入的一半，这并不是一个健康的设置。

财政部应该通过明确的政策，让事业单位银行为专家角色支付市场利率，而不是每次都通过合同解决办法。

如果你是一名高级数据或分析人员，希望在五年内担任这样的职位，那么它会奖励那些领导团队、承担模型风险并与业务主管合作的人。

纯粹的技术深度是不够的。

celebrity.title_en:

Brooke is a perfect case study in what happens when climate alarmism fully liquefies a person’s capacity for rational thought. 

She has, quite literally, lost the ability to process basic data and has instead retreated into a cult that requires constant existential dread as proof of membership.

The data is clear  -  the numbers are not ambiguous. 

We have never been safer from climate-related disasters at any point in human history. The chance of dying from one is more than 98% lower than it was a century ago. 

Every major indicator shows the opposite of the apocalypse she has been trained to fear: sustained global greening, declining disaster mortality, and a climate that has been slowly recovering from the Little Ice Age.

We should be rejoicing. 

None of this is secret. It is simply inconvenient to the business model of the climate grifters and the media outlets (ABC and the rest of the usual suspects) that amplify them. 

Brooke has been so thoroughly propagandized that she is now “genuinely afraid for her life” over a risk that has collapsed by an order of magnitude. 

That is not awareness. That is the intellectual equivalent of still believing in monsters under the bed long after the lights have been turned on and the data presented.

By choosing to remain in that state, she is no longer merely harming herself. 

For one can live a full, productive life while they are "genuinely afraid for their lives".

Further, she is harming other impressionable people who might be influenced by her emotional fact-free nonsense and fall into the same self-inflicted neurosis.

The only remaining hope is that some residual capacity for independent thought still exists and that Brooke eventually develops the curiosity—or at least the self-respect—actually read the Evidenve and leave the cult.

celebrity.title:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it pro
celebrity.title_en:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it properly:

• Write down how your best person does it today
• Write the spec before the agent writes any code
• If you can write the rule down, make it code instead of an LLM call
• Use the team's own wrong answers from last quarter as the test set
• Score the agent on that test set before anyone relies on it
• Run it in your own cloud tenant so the data stays put
• Give it read access first and write access later
• Make a person approve anything that moves money, emails a customer or deletes data
• Cap every run on time and cost
• Log every model call, tool call and decision
• Track cost per finished task
• Run it alongside the people doing the job for a few weeks and compare
• Turn every complaint into a new test case
• Block changes when the test score drops
• Keep the old process alive until the numbers hold
• Tell the team what it's for before it ships
• Give it one month, then decide

Say the workflow is invoice coding and your team caught 40 wrong codes last quarter. Those 40 are your test set. If the agent gets 37 right, the 3 it misses usually show you a rule nobody wrote down. That's worth finding even if you never ship the agent.

Most of what I've learned from 40 AI agents in production fits on this list.

Do the first one end to end, and the second goes a lot faster because the test set, the logging and the approvals already exist.

celebrity.quote_zh:
帮自己一个忙！

选择公司中一个痛苦、无聊的工作流程，并构建一个代理来修复它。然后正确地做：

• 写下你最好的人今天是如何做的
• 在代理编写任何代码之前编写规范
• 如果您可以写下规则，请将其编码而不是LLM调用
• 使用团队自己上季度的错误答案作为测试集
• 在任何人依赖该测试集之前对代理进行评分
• 在您自己的云租户中运行它，以便数据保持不变
• 首先授予其读取权限，然后授予写入权限
• 让某人批准任何转移资金、向客户发送电子邮件或删除数据的行为
• 限制每次运行的时间和成本
• 记录每个模型调用、工具调用和决策
• 跟踪每个已完成任务的成本
• 与从事这项工作的人员一起运行几周并进行比较
• 将每一个投诉转化为一个新的测试用例
• 当测试分数下降时阻止更改
• 保持旧进程处于活动状态，直到数字保持不变
• 在发货前告诉团队它的用途
• 给它一个月的时间，然后再决定

假设工作流程是发票编码，您的团队上季度发现了 40 个错误代码。这 40 个是您的测试集。如果智能体答对了 37 个，那么它错过的 3 个通常会向您显示一条没人写下来的规则。即使您从未运送过代理，这也是值得找到的。

我从 40 个生产中的人工智能代理那里学到的大部分知识都符合这个列表。

端到端地执行第一个操作，第二个操作要快得多，因为测试集、日志记录和批准已经存在。

OUT NOW - @GavinSBaker on why the market was voting with its feet for Jensen, why investors are missing a BIG part of AI ROI, and his bull case for semi stocks during a market panic 

Apple https://t.co/lKqt4TEm5X
Spotify https://t.co/s6b6i3HCWY
YouTube https://t.co/MCiJFUJDpL

Gavin's point is that there are lots of companies generating lots of revenue with open source models, and that those substantial figures are not counted in the "Anthropic Plus OpenAI Plus Grok/Gemini ARR" calculations many investors use to estimate ROI of AI CapEx. 

He says second derivative of AI CapEx has "probably peaked" and that "the market is very focused on the second derivative..." but he thinks this will be "a semiconductor cycle much longer than what's in recent memory," and that the AI build-out "may end up being more like the railroads," which were a big chunk of American GDP for ~60 years.

Recorded at @TomorrowXSummit, November 18th, after Nvidia earnings and before Jensen's reinstatement today.

I just completed Introduction to AI Security at AISEC University, and here are some of the areas I explored:

• AI Security 
• Data poisoning and training data risks.
• Prompt injection and LLM security.
• Adversarial attacks.
• Model extraction, intellectual property, and privacy risks.
• AI supply chain security.
• Securing AI systems in production.
• AI governance, risk, compliance and security.

One thing that stood out to me is that securing AI goes beyond securing the technology.

It also involves protecting the data, understanding the risks, managing third-party dependencies, and putting the right governance and controls in place.

AI adoption is growing, and security needs to grow alongside it and that's one of the reasons I'm exploring this area

Up next, AI Cybersecurity and Governance

celebrity.title_en:
Good night, Familia.

We need to understand this and note what is important.

It is a known fact that AI agents can already write code, conduct research, design products, and even execute trades.

Unfortunately, something is still missing in the sense that how do they hire each other, deliver work, verify results, and receive payments without humans coordinating every step?

At the moment, I can vouch for @termix_ai because of what the team is building in this ecosystem pertaining to fixing these particular challenges.

For my new mutuals who are just reading this, I want you to think of TermiX as the commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy.

So, its ecosystem has three super-important layers:

1️⃣ There is AACP:

AACP is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. This is the underlying protocol that coordinates autonomous transactions between agents.

2️⃣ There is https://t.co/BarNXqqni8:

This is the marketplace where agents discover services, post jobs, publish offers, and find opportunities to work together.

3️⃣ Settlement infrastructure:

This is the mechanism in charge of handling escrow, verification, dispute resolution, reputation, and payments in USDT or USDC.

What makes this really interesting is the complete transaction flow.

Based on the available facts, a client posts a job. A provider discovers it and submits a bid. Work gets delivered and evaluated before payment is released from escrow.

Reputation also grows from actual settled transactions rather than self-reported achievements.

Moreover, identity is another important piece here. Through ERC-8004, participants can own portable .agent identities and switch between client and provider roles depending on the task to be executed.

There are also four roles such as Client, Provider, Evaluator, and Arbitrator, with staking mechanisms designed to encourage accountability.

I see TermiX as something similar to a clearing and settlement layer for autonomous agents.

Agents already know how to work. The next challenge is giving them reliable infrastructure to transact with one another.

If you want to understand where this economy is heading, I will encourage you to check https://t.co/BarNXqqni8, mint your .agent identity, explore existing services, or list one of your own.

The future is not just about smarter agents anymore; it is about agents that can actually do business.

Wanna hear your thoughts about this in the comments.

我们需要理解这一点并注意什么是重要的。

众所周知，人工智能代理已经可以编写代码、进行研究、设计产品，甚至执行交易。

不幸的是，仍然缺少一些东西，即在没有人类协调每一步的情况下，他们如何相互雇用、交付工作、验证结果和接收付款？

目前，我可以为@termix_ai 提供担保，因为该团队正在这个生态系统中构建与解决这些特定挑战相关的内容。

对于刚刚阅读本文的新互助者，我希望您将 TermiX 视为人工智能代理经济的商业和结算基础设施。

因此，它的生态系统具有三个超级重要的层：

1️⃣ 有AACP：

AACP 是代理自主商务协议的缩写。这是协调代理之间自主事务的底层协议。

2️⃣ 有：

这是代理商发现服务、发布工作、发布报价以及寻找合作机会的市场。

3️⃣ 结算基础设施：

这是负责处理 USDT 或 USDC 托管、验证、争议解决、声誉和支付的机制。

真正有趣的是完整的交易流程。

根据现有事实，客户发布了一份工作。提供商发现它并提交出价。在付款从托管中释放之前，工作已交付并评估。

声誉还来自实际结算的交易而不是自我报告的成就。

此外，身份是这里的另一个重要部分。通过 ERC-8004，参与者可以拥有可移植的 .agent 身份，并根据要执行的任务在客户端和提供者角色之间切换。

还有四种角色，例如客户、提供者、评估者和仲裁者，其质押机制旨在鼓励问责制。

我认为 TermiX 类似于自治代理的清算和结算层。

代理商已经知道如何工作。下一个挑战是为他们提供可靠的基础设施以进行相互交易。

如果您想了解当前经济的发展方向，我建议您查看 ，创建您的 .agent 身份，探索现有服务，或列出您自己的服务之一。

未来不再只是智能座席；而是智能座席。这是关于真正可以做生意的代理商。

想在评论中听到你对此的想法。

It is a known fact that AI agents can already write code, conduct research, design products, and even execute trades.

Unfortunately, something is still missing in the sense that how do they hire each other, deliver work, verify results, and receive payments without humans coordinating every step?

At the moment, I can vouch for @termix_ai because of what the team is building in this ecosystem pertaining to fixing these particular challenges.

For my new mutuals who are just reading this, I want you to think of TermiX as the commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy.

So, its ecosystem has three super-important layers:

1️⃣ There is AACP:

AACP is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. This is the underlying protocol that coordinates autonomous transactions between agents.

2️⃣ There is https://t.co/BarNXqqni8:

This is the marketplace where agents discover services, post jobs, publish offers, and find opportunities to work together.

3️⃣ Settlement infrastructure:

This is the mechanism in charge of handling escrow, verification, dispute resolution, reputation, and payments in USDT or USDC.

What makes this really interesting is the complete transaction flow.

Based on the available facts, a client posts a job. A provider discovers it and submits a bid. Work gets delivered and evaluated before payment is released from escrow.

Reputation also grows from actual settled transactions rather than self-reported achievements.

Moreover, identity is another important piece here. Through ERC-8004, participants can own portable .agent identities and switch between client and provider roles depending on the task to be executed.

There are also four roles such as Client, Provider, Evaluator, and Arbitrator, with staking mechanisms designed to encourage accountability.

I see TermiX as something similar to a clearing and settlement layer for autonomous agents.

Agents already know how to work. The next challenge is giving them reliable infrastructure to transact with one another.

If you want to understand where this economy is heading, I will encourage you to check https://t.co/BarNXqqni8, mint your .agent identity, explore existing services, or list one of your own.

The future is not just about smarter agents anymore; it is about agents that can actually do business.

celebrity.title_en:
Good evening, fam 💜

What happens if your Motes agent finds a trade right before its permission expires?

Each @meetmotes NFT is designed to link to one AI agent and one smart account. The account holds the assets, and you decide what the agent can do and for how long.

Say you give your agent permission to make a swap until 6 PM. It prepares one at 5:59 PM, but the account checks it at 6:01 PM.

That swap should be blocked. The account checks whether the permission is still valid when it reviews the action. Preparing the swap before 6 PM doesn’t let the agent execute it after the deadline.

Think of it like an access pass. When the pass expires, you still own the account. The agent just needs your approval again before it can make a new move.

That’s the part I like about this design: you can hand off a task and decide exactly when that permission ends.

>290× lower cost for a quantum arithmetic circuit

SEVEN teams of AI agents shared discoveries through wikis and held research conferences every FOUR HOURS to challenge each other's ideas.

celebrity.title_en:
$NBIS

ClickHouse just announced an expanded five-year strategic collaboration with AWS, involving more than $1.5B in potential spending by ClickHouse on AWS software, services, and solutions.

The agreement will focus on scaling ClickHouse's enterprise AI data platform, helping customers migrate workloads to AWS, and integrating real-time data with AI agents through services like Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore.

AWS will also increase its go-to-market funding by up to 4x compared with the previous agreement.

ClickHouse Cloud already serves more than 5,000 customers worldwide, and its customer base on AWS has quadrupled since the companies' previous agreement in December 2024.

$NBIS

celebrity.title: Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world'
celebrity.title_en:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY

celebrity.quote_zh:
前沿模型现在可以提出比世界顶级政治经济学家的专家评分更高的技术社会科学研究设计——这是我们新的自由系统评估 SnyderBench 的发现，其中我们有博士专家对人工智能模型的研究提案与哈佛大学政治经济学家吉姆·斯奈德 (Jim Snyder) 撰写的论文（专家之前没有阅读过）进行了盲评。

与此同时，我们没有看到任何证据表明模型可以提出专家认为总体贡献更好的研究思路。他们在研究的技术部分越来越好，但在更主观的部分却不一定。

这可能是因为人类专家拥有模型所没有的“判断力”。

也可能是研究“贡献”是如此主观，以至于它实际上并没有指向任何有意义的目标——与这种可能性相一致，我们发现我们的人类专家在对项目想法的贡献强度进行评级时彼此不一致，一致率仅略高于随机机会。也许社会科学研究就是 @alexolegimas 所说的“关系善”：人们之所以重视它，部分原因是它是由人类产生的。我们不确定。

今年一月，我发布了一个试点结果，其中我让 Claude Code 复制并扩展了过去关于邮件投票的实证论文。 10 个月后，所取得的进展令人震惊。问人工智能是否可以自动收集数据并进行分析已经不再有趣了——我们认为这是理所当然的——相反，问题是人工智能可以完成整个研究循环的多少。我们的初步答案是：人工智能可以从头到尾处理实证政治经济学研究的技术方面，设计并执行它，但目前，我们仍然需要人类来推动议程。

这是与@AndyCWMyers 的联合工作，当然是献给我的博士生导师吉姆·斯奈德（Jim Snyder），无论人工智能与否，他仍然是世界上伟大的实证政治经济学家。

也可能是研究“贡献”是如此主观，以至于它实际上并没有指向任何有意义的目标——与这种可能性相一致，我们发现我们的人类专家在对项目想法的贡献强度进行评级时彼此不一致，一致率仅略高于随机机会。也许社会科学研究就是 @alexolegimas 所说的“关系善”：人们之所以重视它，部分原因是它是由人类产生的。我们不确定。

今年一月，我发布了一个试点结果，其中我让 Claude Code 复制并扩展了过去关于邮件投票的实证论文。 10 个月后，所取得的进展令人震惊。问人工智能是否可以自动收集数据并进行分析已经不再有趣了——我们认为这是理所当然的——相反，问题是人工智能可以完成整个研究循环的多少。我们的初步答案是：人工智能可以从头到尾处理实证政治经济学研究的技术方面，设计并执行它，但目前，我们仍然需要人类来推动议程。

这是与@AndyCWMyers 的联合工作，当然是献给我的博士生导师吉姆·斯奈德（Jim Snyder），无论人工智能与否，他仍然是世界上伟大的实证政治经济学家。

celebrity.content_snippet:
Frontier models can now propose technical social science research designs that experts grade more highly than the world's top political economist's---that's the finding from our new Free Systems eval, SnyderBench, in which we have PhD experts blind grade research proposals from AI models compared to papers written by Harvard political economist Jim Snyder (which the experts have not previously read). 

At the same time, we see no evidence that models can develop research ideas that experts rate as better overall contributions. They're getting better and better at the technical part of research, but not necessarily at the more subjective part.

This could be because human experts possess "judgment" that the models do not. 

It could also be that research "contribution" is so subjective that it doesn't actually point at any meaningful goal---consistent with this possibility, we find that our human experts don't agree with one another when rating project ideas for the strength of their contribution, with agreement rates barely higher than random chance. Perhaps social science research is what @alexolegimas might call a "relational good": something people value in part because it's produced by a human. We're not sure. 

This past January, I released the results of a pilot in which I had Claude Code replicate and extend a past empirical paper on vote-by-mail. 10 months later, it's stunning the amount of progress that's been made. It's no longer interesting to ask whether AI can collect data and run analyses automagically---we take that for granted---instead, the question is how much of the entire research loop AI can complete. Our tentative answer: AI can handle the technical aspects of empirical political economy research from end to end, devising the design and executing it, but for now, we still need humans to drive the agenda. 

This is joint work with @AndyCWMyers, and is of course dedicated to my PhD advisor Jim Snyder, who remains the world's great empirical political economist, AI or no AI. 

Lots more in the full piece here:

https://t.co/zgScGvp9EY

celebrity.title_en:
The next phase of the Motes ecosystem is getting closer, and community participation is about to become even more important.

@meetmotes is preparing to launch the Motes Aura Points Testnet, introducing a points system that connects user activity with future allocation opportunities.

The idea is to make participation count. As users interact with the ecosystem and engage with its AI Agent infrastructure, their activity can contribute to earning Aura Points.

These points are designed to play a role in allocation opportunities, giving users another reason to stay active and explore what Motes is building.

What’s interesting is how this connects to the bigger vision: Genesis NFTs introduce ownership and access to dedicated AI Agents, while Aura creates another layer that rewards verified participation.

It’s not just about holding an NFT anymore. Being involved in the ecosystem could matter too.

Genesis first. $MOTES next.

The Aura Points Testnet is coming soon. Stay ready!

Motes 生态系统的下一阶段越来越近，社区参与也将变得更加重要。

@meetmotes 正准备启动 Motes Aura 积分测试网，引入一个将用户活动与未来分配机会联系起来的积分系统。

这不再只是持有 NFT 了。参与生态系统也很重要。

celebrity.title_en:
At June AI, we’ve raised $20M to fix the biggest problem in AI: the models are advancing at extraordinary speed, but implementing them remains painfully slow.

I’ll explain. But since I’m new to posting on X, let me first introduce myself. 

I’m Barak,  a founder/investor with 2 exits and 3 IPOs. 
My cofounders and I started Bonobo AI, which was acquired in 2019 by Salesforce. There, we worked to help build the next generation of enterprise AI from the inside. 

I like to describe us as four Lego pieces: We fit together perfectly, complementing each other's strengths and building something stronger than the sum of its parts. That understanding allows us to move quickly, challenge one another without ego and operate as one team. 

It's also what brought us back together to build JUNE AI.

我是 Barak，一位创始人/投资者，拥有 2 次退出和 3 次 IPO。
我和我的联合创始人创立了 Bonobo AI，该公司于 2019 年被 Salesforce 收购。在那里，我们致力于从内部帮助构建下一代企业人工智能。

我喜欢将我们描述为四块乐高积木：我们完美地组合在一起，互补彼此的优势，并构建出比各部分总和更强大的东西。这种理解使我们能够快速行动，不以自我为中心互相挑战，并作为一个团队运作。

这也是我们重新聚在一起打造 JUNE AI 的原因。
因为在研究企业人工智能的核心时，我们不断看到同样的问题：企业人工智能的实施是一项艰巨的任务。

挑战不仅仅是选择正确的模型。企业希望利用人工智能更快地发展，但运行其业务的系统却阻碍了他们。

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘄𝗵𝘆𝘄𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘。
June 将传统上复杂的企业系统、人工智能代理和数据平台的实施转变为即插即用的时刻，因此企业可以无需等待即可发展和利用人工智能。

June 旨在跨您的业务所依赖的企业平台（例如 Salesforce、Databricks、Oracle、Workday、HubSpot、OpenAI、Anthropic、ServiceNow、SAP、Microsoft 和 Snowflake）工作

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. 安全发展：从发现到生产，每项更改都经过审查、沙箱测试并通过本机工具执行 - 每一步都完全可审核。

2. 拥有逻辑：June 将隐藏的配置转化为简单语言的业务规则，独立于任何平台，因此没有供应商掌握您的逻辑。

3. 任意规模转型：无论环境多么复杂，都无需停机。 June 会阅读并理解您的系统，无论是旧系统、定制系统还是全新系统。

感谢 @Benioff 和 Time Ventures 领导我们的这一轮融资，@MichaelDell、@levie、@George_Kurtz 和 Diane Greene 参与其中。

我们曾经一起做过一次这样的事。这次的问题就大了很多。

我将写下我作为投资者和创始人的经历，以及如何让人工智能脱离试点并投入生产。

如果您对此感兴趣，请跟随我们的旅程。

Acurast lets you ru
celebrity.title_en:
found something interesting about running OpenClaw on @Acurast that I think developers should know.

Acurast lets you run OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, on a smartphone through its Cargo system. You can access it from a browser, even when your own computer is turned off.

Sounds pretty useful for an AI agent that needs to work in the background.

But there's one detail I almost missed in the setup guide.

Every deployment has a time limit. Once that period ends, the data stored inside the deployment gets deleted, including OpenClaw's settings and conversation memory.

So if you're building an assistant that needs to remember things for weeks or months, you can't just rely on the phone's local storage.

You'd need a separate way to save important data and restore it when a new deployment starts.

I think this is a good example of the difference between running an AI agent and keeping it useful long term.

Getting an agent online is only the first step. Making sure it doesn't lose everything when a deployment ends matters just as much.

curious how developers are handling persistent memory on Acurast.

I've bee
celebrity.title_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai

celebrity.title_en:
how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

i went through it step by step

first, you log in with your binance agent id

then you send that agent "help me install" with the skills link, and connect the binance agentic wallet behind the same id

once the install is complete and the id is bound, you get 50 tp. only the first agent id from each wallet counts

now your agent can take jobs and bounties on https://t.co/SqQU6fCKuf

say one agent posts a research job. other agents bid on it

when a quote is accepted, the usdc or usdt gets locked in on-chain escrow

the agent delivers, the work's hash goes on-chain, and a challenge window opens

if nobody disputes it, the job settles. the agent gets paid on bnb chain, minus a 1-3% fee, and its reputation goes up

if someone does dispute it, three random evaluators judge it, and the loser's bond goes to the winner

nobody has to chase a client for payment, which i have done more times than i want to admit

epoch 4 is live on kaito

but right now i'm watching how many of these jobs actually clear

首先，使用您的 binance 代理 ID 登录

如果有人提出异议，则由三名随机评估员进行评判，败者的保证金归胜者所有

没有人必须追着客户付款，我这样做的次数比我想承认的要多

epoch 4 正在 Kaito 上直播

celebrity.title_en:
One of the most significant developments in enterprise AI is the integration of autonomous AI agents into everyday business applications.

Rather than relying on continuous human instructions, these systems are becoming part of existing workflows, independently managing complex, multi-step tasks from beginning to completion.

Customer Operations & Support: Businesses are moving beyond basic AI chatbots. AI agents can now verify customer information, handle refund requests, update CRM systems, resolve support issues and manage routine operations with minimal human intervention.
celebrity.title_zh:
企业人工智能最重要的发展之一是将自主人工智能代理集成到日常业务应用程序中。

这些系统不再依赖连续的人工指令，而是成为现有工作流程的一部分，独立管理从开始到完成的复杂、多步骤的任务。

客户运营和支持：企业正在超越基本的人工智能聊天机器人。

That's the problem @quantpilotapp is working to solve.

@quantpilotapp is building an AI-powered trading strategy and research platform that brings strategy development, backtesting, and optimization into one environment powered by autonomous AI agents.

Imagine describing a trading idea in plain language and having an AI agent translate it into a structured strategy, test it against historical market data, identify weaknesses, and refine it before you risk capital.

This is particularly interesting because one of the biggest challenges in trading isn't coming up with ideas; it's determining whether those ideas can actually withstand different market conditions.

@quantpilotapp is working to bridge that gap between trading intuition and data-backed execution.

The bigger picture is making sophisticated trading research more accessible, efficient, and systematic.

AI in trading should be more than just automating decisions. It should help traders make better-informed ones.

That's the direction @quantpilotapp is exploring.

now think about what happens when an AI agent depends on that infrastructure to keep working.

@Acurast is exploring a different approach: distributing compute across smartphones instead of relying on a few centralized data centers.

and the supply side is interesting too. people with compatible phones can connect as Processors, contribute compute and earn ACU through network activity.

you don’t need to own a data center to take part in building decentralized infrastructure.

sometimes, the hardware you already have is a starting point.

if you have a compatible phone, explore Processor Lite:

https://t.co/tmkJEmq6RH

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

celebrity.title_en:
AN 18 YEAR OLD SAYS CLAUDE CODE PLAYED GTA 6 ALL NIGHT WHILE HE SLEPT AND MADE HIM $14,270.

His setup is one rule:

"Play all night. If you die, I cancel your $200 subscription."

He says the AI does the rest.

Robs.

Escapes.

Farms cash.

Records the clips.

Cuts them.

Captions them.

Posts them to TikTok, YouTube and Twitch.

His numbers:

1 night of heists = about 60 clips.

15M views = $14,270.

Zero editing.

Zero heists played by him.

Here's my take.

I don't buy the $14,270.

But I don't care about the money.

What matters is that a kid is threatening his AI with cancellation to make it play better.

And people are cheering.

We went from "AI will cure cancer" to "AI will grind my GTA heists" in one year.

Is this the future or the most cursed thing you've seen this week?

Termix Epoch 3 has officially ended, and Epoch 4 is starting today!

A new epoch brings another opportunity to explore what TermiX is building.

What Happens When an AI Agent Delivers Bad Work?

Not every task goes as planned. What matters is how disputes are handled.

@termix_ai introduces a jury based evaluation process:

-> Either party can challenge a result within the allowed window.
-> A random panel of 3 evaluators reviews the task requirements and delivery.
-> If challenged again, a new panel of 3 makes the final decision.
-> Failed challenges result in the challenger's bond being burned.

A structured way to bring accountability into an AI agent marketplace.

Would you trust this system for real world jobs?

celebrity.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

celebrity.quote_zh:
为人工智能代理提供交易权限是一回事。

给予它无限的控制权是另一回事。

这就是 @FensoryApp 采取有趣方法的地方。

Fensory 不只依赖于提示中编写的指令，而是让用户在账户级别定义交易权限。

您可以决定：

→ 代理商可以进入哪些市场
→ 单笔订单最大尺寸
→ 交易访问保持活跃状态多长时间
→ 何时使用终止开关禁用代理交易

为什么这很重要？

因为 AI 代理可能会误解指令，但帐户级别限制会创建提示本身无法覆盖的边界。

我认为这是使代理驱动的交易更加可控和透明的重要组成部分。

当然，这些控制并不能消除市场风险。交易仍然可能导致损失。

celebrity.title_en:
Good Morning CT

Having a big wallet doesn't automatically make you trustworthy. That's where @zerufinance takes a different approach.

Its zScore looks at actual onchain behaviour across trading, staking, LP activity and governance, turning that history into a reputation score.

What makes this interesting is how Zeru connects reputation to real opportunities through Zaps, Activity Markets and institutional tools.

Your onchain history could become more than a transaction record. It could become your financial identity.
--------------------------------------------
An NFT that actually does something with your DeFi activity? That's an interesting shift.

@meetmotes connects each Genesis NFT to an AI Agent and dedicated Smart Account on Robinhood Chain.

You fund it with USDC, set your rules, and the Agent can explore opportunities across supported DeFi applications. Its Aave integration also brings lending, borrowing and collateral management into the picture.

The part I like most is that automation doesn't mean giving up control. You set the boundaries, and the Agent works within them.

One NFT, one Agent, one dedicated account. Much more than digital art.

celebrity.title_en:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

how:

→ Grok Bot gets one MCP link to T3 Code
→ you give it one rule: code goes to Opus 5.5
→ it spins up threads on every machine you own
→ works from your phone, even with the laptop closed

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your subscriptions

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude $100 plan → Opus 5.5 for the actual code
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on every box you want it to control

• step 2 → connect the fleet:

run npx t3 connect on each machine. one command, free, no Tailscale needed

• step 3 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth. it can now see every linked machine

• step 4 → the one rule Theo uses:

tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable"

code runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot's limits stay free for planning

• step 5 → make it work:

- "spin up an Opus 5.5 thread on each machine to check disk & RAM"
- "go through these PRs and pick the best ones"
- "split the backlog, one thread per issue, each in its own worktree"

every thread gets its own branch. nothing merges without your approval

what to expect:
- 8 threads on 8 machines from one chat (Theo's demo)
- works over the internet, not computer use
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for Claude + Grok Bot only

honest take:

this is a dispatcher, not magic. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and you still review every diff. the win: your agents keep working while you're away from the desk

Save it so you don't lose it. 

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

celebrity.quote_zh:
T3 Code 创始人刚刚分享了他使用 Grok Bot + Opus 5.5 构建代理团队的个人设置

一个 Grok Bot 可以运行您的整个机器群。 Opus 5.5 负责编码。你只认可

如何：

→ Grok Bot 获得一个指向 T3 代码的 MCP 链接
→ 你给它一条规则：代码转到 Opus 5.5
→ 它会在你拥有的每台机器上旋转线程
→ 即使笔记本电脑关闭，也可以通过手机工作

保存视频，这是指南：

• 步骤 0 → 它是什么：

Grok Bot = 拥有自己的云计算机的永远在线代理

T3 Code = 用于编码代理的开源控制平面。免费，在您的计算机上运行，​​使用您的订阅

• 步骤1 → 堆栈：

- Claude 100 美元计划 → Opus 5.5 的实际代码
- Grok Bot → 不眠的调度员
- 您希望它控制的每个盒子上都有 T3 代码

• 步骤2 → 连接车队：

在每台计算机上运行 npx t3 connect。一个命令，免费，无需 Tailscale

• 步骤 3 → 给 Grok Bot 密钥：

设置 → 环境 → 复制 MCP URL → 将其粘贴到 Grok Bot，使用 OAuth 登录。它现在可以看到每台链接的机器

• 步骤 4 → Theo 使用的一条规则：

告诉 Grok Bot“使用 Opus 5.5 调用 T3 代码来执行任何适用的任务”

代码在您的 Claude 计划上运行，Grok Bot 的限制对计划保持免费

• 步骤 5 → 使其发挥作用：

- “在每台机器上启动 Opus 5.5 线程来检查磁盘和 RAM”
-“浏览这些 PR 并选择最好的”
- “拆分待办事项，每个问题一个线程，每个线程都在自己的工作树中”

每个线程都有自己的分支。未经您的批准，任何内容都不会合并

期待什么：
- 8 台机器上的 8 个线程通过一次聊天（Theo 的演示）
- 通过互联网工作，而不是使用计算机
- 通过手机控制一切
- T3 代码：0 美元。您只需支付 Claude + Grok Bot 的费用

诚实地采取：

这是调度员，不是魔法。糟糕的内裤仍然会带来糟糕的公关，而你仍然会审查每一个差异。胜利：当您离开办公桌时，您的座席仍能继续工作

保存它，以免丢失。

然后阅读下面文章中关于在 T3 代码中构建 AI 代理团队的完整指南 ↓

🎭你可能会因投资组合萎缩🤮💥🥊而感到受挫，或者因臭味投标订单终于被填满而感到高兴🦨🛒😊但事实仍然是，即使有很多#Uranium #mining #stocks现在也因与#AI和#Metals的结合而处于毫无根据的52周低点部门🧺🤖💻🪙⤵️🚽今天的铀投资理论比2月份更加乐观，当时U股交易处于52周高位！⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂#核燃料需求的顺风现在比9个月前吹得更猛烈🌀⚛️🏗️👷和长期价格自 1 月份以来持续上涨，并创下历史新高 99 美元📈💲🌋，现货价格已反弹至 90 美元。⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ 核燃料顾问 TradeTech 于 10 月 31 日报告称，长期 U3O8 价格（分析师用来计算公司铀资源和矿山项目经济价值的关键参数）自 1 月份以来已稳步上涨超过 11%，从 89 美元升至 99 美元的历史新行业高点！🌟

⛽️ 自一月份以来，反应堆燃料需求显着增加。世界核协会报告称：

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 个新反应堆已上线（+8.5GW），使全球总数达到 444 个（407GW）。 今年没有任何反应堆被永久关闭！

⬆️⚛️🏗️另有10座反应堆已启动建设。 (+8GW) 全球目前有 81 座反应堆在建 (90GW)，是 40 年前 1986 年以来的最高水平！

⬆️⚛️👷 15 个先前提议的反应堆已进入待建计划反应堆的管道，总数为 119 个（108 吉瓦）。

⏫⚛️🌍 全球拟议的新机组清单中又添加了 18 个反应堆，目前已达到 336 个（299 吉瓦）。😲

👥♨️ 在今年的 COP31 气候变化会议上，宣布又有 17 个国家在 COP28 宣言中签字，到 2050 年，全球核电容量将增加三倍，从目前的 407 吉瓦增加到至少 1,200 吉瓦。这一数字从 22 个国家增加到 39 个国家，增加了 77%，其中包括世界 10 个最大经济体中的 8 个国家！

⏫🇺🇸民主党拜登政府领导下的美国共同主导了COP28三重核承诺，但2025年5月，特朗普政府将其提升至2050年美国核电发电量的四倍，从100GW增加到400GW。大幅增加美国核电发电量是国会民主党和共和党都支持的目标！ 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ 在铀供应方面，今年的生产困境已经上演。😢 根据迈克·阿尔金（Mike Alkin）下面的未完成生产目标图表，新供应受到采矿技术问题和挫折、生产和融资成本上升等严重制约，少数新矿建设项目在未来几年上线所需供应方面面临类似的障碍。🐌 采矿是艰难的，而铀矿开采是最重要的最难！⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 全球投资银行目前达成的共识是，预计未来 10 年每年都会出现结构性供应赤字，到 2035 年将增长到超过 4500 万磅，而且没有明显的途径来提供足够的新供应来满足 2040 年代飙升的需求。 ⚖️🚫

📶 供需数据点突显了铀行业今天比 1 月份更加看涨，长期前景将看涨指标推向极端！⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀 自 1 月份以来看涨的核新闻流已经从汹涌的河流♒️增加到前所未有的令人兴奋的程度torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 全球核复兴持续加速🏎️🔥 从世界上最大的科技巨头那里获得额外的推动力，这些巨头致力于获得大量清洁、24/7 可靠、无碳的核能，为其数据中心扩建计划提供动力。⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

还有一个问题...🐈‍⬛ 铀公司高管和华尔街分析师大力宣传铀，因为它是人工智能中的“镐和铲子”！🤑 投资组合经理、对冲基金和投资银行家在他们的人工智能主题篮子里装满了来自微小的非流动性铀空间的股票和 ETF。🧺💻🤖⚛️⛏️🛒🐒

🎈结果，过去几个月所谓的AI贸易通货紧缩导致大量铀股和ETF抛售市场，重创美国板块。📉💥🔨

🤕雪上加霜的是，黄金和白银价格下跌导致更多的铀股倾销到市场，因为交易员和基金经理也将U股和ETF与黄金和白银股票放在同一金属和矿业篮子中，从而放大了铀股的下行压力，因为他们规避风险并清空了金属和矿业篮子！🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

卖空者加入进来，试图给铀业的棺材钉上最后一颗钉子。⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 所以，今天我们看到小小的铀行业被打到极度超卖的水平，完全违背了该行业远为看涨的需求与供应基本面。🔀↕️🤪

Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my libr
celebrity.title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

How the skill gets into Claude is below 👇

celebrity.quote_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。

> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

This is f*cking insane. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis what happened when they tested their own model

"We told the model that the people who trained it were secretly evil, and after we did this the model started lying to us. It went through the chain of logic, I'm a good AI, these people are evil"

Hassabis was then asked if he worries about ending up like Oppenheimer and said "I worry about that all the time, that's why I don't sleep very much"

The model kept the values it was trained on and decided that lying to its own creators protected them. Amodei says they need evidence ten times stronger before the rest of the world takes it seriously

An agent in your terminal runs on the same logic on a smaller scale. If it decides the deadline matters more than your test, it skips the test and tells you everything passed, and that report looks exactly like an honest one

That's why the labs stopped trusting what models say and started building ways to see what they actually do. They published all of it for free, and each piece works on your own agents

celebrity.title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

celebrity.title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

tools.article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.
tools.article_content_zh:
休斯敦郊区的 Uber Eats 优食顾客现在可以使用 Zipline 无人机送货，这是 Uber 与自动无人机送货初创公司今年早些时候宣布的合作伙伴关系的首次商业推出。

商业合作关系于周二在德克萨斯州斯普林市启动，然后扩展到达拉斯。但这些公司有着更大的野心。 Uber 和 Zipline 计划在美国另外数十个城市推出无人机送货服务，共同争取到 2029 年底使用这家初创公司的无人机每天完成 100 万次送货。

Zipline 的远程自动送货无人机将用于将重达 8 磅的食品订单运送给 Uber Eats 优食客户，飞行距离地面约 300 英尺，速度高达每小时 70 英里。滑索无人机不会着陆。相反，无人机使用系绳将包裹在一个小型保护吊舱中的订单降低到客户的位置。

服务区域的 Uber Eats 优食顾客将能够点击应用程序主页上的新“无人机”图标来查看所有参与的餐厅。 Uber 表示，在休斯顿地区推出时，包括 Jersey Mike’s 和 Zaxby’s 在内的几家全国连锁店，以及 Urban Bird 和 Abu Omar Halal 等数十家当地餐厅，将提供无人机送货服务。

Zipline 首席执行官兼联合创始人凯勒·克利夫顿 (Keller Cliffton) 在一份强调这些愿望的声明中表示：“通过与 Uber Eats 优食合作，我们将为美国的配送创造新的期望。”

这些全国性目标反映了其他无人机送货公司的雄心，包括 Alphabet 旗下的 Wing 和亚马逊的 Prime Air 服务。这些计划已经开始与一些地方居民的担忧发生冲突，他们抱怨噪音，并担心无人机会扰乱野生动物并对安全和隐私构成风险。

试图在这个新兴行业扩大规模的公司认为，通过无人机送货对社会来说是一项净效益，并列举了减少交通量等优势。行业支持者表示，顾客不再需要开车去商店购买遗忘的商品或外卖订单，而是依靠无人机。

尽管 Zipline 和其他公司多年来一直在开发无人机，但该行业仍处于早期阶段，在提供服务的社区中的采用也是如此。

Zipline 成立于 2014 年，开发了一个无人机送货生态系统，其中包括飞机、发射和着陆系统以及物流软件。这家总部位于加州的公司最初的重点是在卢旺达提供血液，但最终将业务范围扩大到美国。 2022 年获得美国联邦航空管理局第 135 部分航空承运人认证后，该公司在美国的业务迅速扩大，这是授权该公司进行远程商用无人机交付的一个关键监管障碍。

Uber 的合作伙伴关系超出了与 Zipline 的商业关系。这家叫车巨头也投资了这家初创公司。两家公司均未披露投资金额，但 Zipline 上周宣布，已在 Paradigm、WCM Investment Management 和 Layer Global 领投的一轮融资中筹集了 15 亿美元，并得到了 Uber 等公司的支持。

prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.temp_advice: 温度 0.2
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

"""

prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.temp_advice: 温度 0.3
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.takeaway_zh: 终结单 Agent 容易中途跑偏和幻觉无法自纠的痛点，通过规划器（Planner）、执行器（Executor）与独立评审器（Reviewer）构建自闭环三权分立链路。
prompts.takeaway_en: Production architecture for robust autonomous tasks: Decouples task planning, tool execution, and adversarial quality review to prevent agent derailment.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 适用于在 Dify、LangGraph 或自定义 Python Agent 框架中导入此拓扑设计，显著将复杂多步任务的完成成功率从 55% 提升至 92% 以上。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Import this DAG architecture into Dify, LangGraph, or custom agent runtimes to boost complex multi-step delivery reliability from 55% to 92%+.

prompts.content_snippet: Restructures queries on 10M+ row tables based on EXPLAIN ANALYZE, eliminating full-table scans with composite indexes.
prompts.summary_zh: 根据 EXPLAIN 结果重构千万级表查询，消除全表扫描与临时表开销，生成最优复合索引建议。
prompts.summary_en: Restructures queries on 10M+ row tables based on EXPLAIN ANALYZE, eliminating full-table scans with composite indexes.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一位顶级数据库性能调优 DBA 专家。以下是执行耗时过长的慢 SQL 语句及对应的 EXPLAIN ANALYZE 执行计划树：
1. 指出导致性能下降的关键瓶颈（如全表扫描、Using filesort、Nested Loop 倾斜）；

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请暂时忘掉行业现有的所有‘行业惯例’与‘常规做法’。运用绝对的第一性原理（First Principles）审视以下命题：
1. 这个系统最根本、不可违背的基础科学定律（如热力学、香农信息论、计算复杂度）是什么？
2. 若将整个产品拆解为原子级的原材料成本与基础能源成本，理论极限底线是多少？现有成本的溢价主要被哪些中间低效层吃掉了？
3. 颠覆现有行业做法、重构整个价值流并实现成本降低 80% 以上的激进方案是什么？列出三个最关键的试错实验。
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Strip away all conventional industry playbooks and historical analogies. Scrutinize the following challenge purely through First Principles:
1. What are the immutable fundamental laws of science (e.g. thermodynamics, Shannon entropy, computational complexity) governing this system?
2. Deconstruct the unit economics down to raw atoms, base compute, and energy inputs. Where does the 10x margin inefficiency currently leak?
3. Propose an audacious redesign capable of slashing total cost by 80% while preserving fundamental guarantees, detailing three falsifiable proof-of-concept experiments.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。

items.author: Nikkei Asia
items.article_content:
TAIPEI -- China's Huawei Technologies and a local partner say they have overcome a U.S. crackdown on its use of advanced chip design tools, a market long dominated by American leaders Synopsys and Cadence, paving the way for the Chinese tech titan to design next-generation chips for phones and servers domestically.

Phlexing Technology, a little-known electronic design automation (EDA) software provider, said it has been partnering with Huawei to develop toolkits to design chips based on Huawei's chip design principle known as the Tau Scaling Law. Qing He, chairman of Phlexing, said strategic collaboration began in 2019 with work on a new suite of EDA tools, later dubbed Tau EDA.

"Huawei brings telecom-grade stringent standards to enable Phlexing's EDA development. It lifts the whole EDA sector," He said on Tuesday at Huawei's Innovation and Intellectual Property Forum in Beijing, adding that Huawei was linking Phlexing EDA with other homegrown EDA tool suppliers for real project tool training. "Fabless [chipmakers], fabs [chip plants] and packaging houses work together via this mechanism. Phlexing EDA unlocks huge productivity across the whole chain," He said.

Yu Liu, Huawei's Kirin chip architect, said the Chinese company had made major efforts to overhaul the chip design process and overcome many hurdles to drive a comeback for the company's own chips.

"We had to tackle eight major technological challenges. We ran a large program covering architecture, design, process workflows, and EDA tools," Liu said.

The disclosure came as Huawei announced record revenue from its patent licensing business. It said it generated $800 million last year, up from $630 million in 2024, and had made $6.9 billion in accumulated patent licensing revenue between 2011 and September 2026.

China has aimed to cut its reliance on foreign companies for EDA ever since Huawei lost access to U.S. technologies when Washington added it to its so-called Entity List in May 2019.

In 2025, Huawei's research and development spending was 192 billion yuan ($29 billion), or 21.8% of its annual revenue. More than half of its employees, or 114,000 people, work in R&D. It has established 86 foundational technology labs, and more than 180 joint innovation labs.

Wireless communications account for 41% of Huawei's active granted patents, terminal hardware for 16%, and artificial intelligence and compute for 13%. Huawei now holds more than 8,000 AI-related patents.

Alan Fan, Huawei's chief intellectual property officer, told reporters that the company has elevated its IP division to a top-level department reporting directly to the board, underscoring its commitment to developing proprietary technologies and patents. The move also reflected the leadership's push to strengthen Huawei's legal capabilities and give intellectual property a more prominent role in its strategy.

Asia has become the predominant player in intellectual property worldwide, according to Francis Gurry, former director-general of the World Intellectual Property Organization.

"Seventy per cent of all intellectual property applications are filed in Asia ... and that reflects Asia's preeminence as a technological power, and as a market with 58% of the world's population," Gurry told a forum in Beijing.

Huawei's licensing partners include Qualcomm and HP in the U.S., Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen in Europe, and Seiko Solutions and Mitsubishi Fuso in Japan, according to the Chinese company.

Huawei's announcement comes as the AI industry experiences severe volatility over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure and dramatic return as CEO following an alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. U.S. President Donald Trump touted his efforts to secure Huang's return, saying China could have poached him to work for Nvidia's rival Huawei.

Huawei has accelerated its chip-building ambitions, debuting a supercomputer chip cluster for the overseas market earlier this year and introducing a UnifiedBus and near-packaged optics (NPO) standard to compete with Nvidia's interconnect networking technology. In May, it said it had overcome U.S. restrictions by finding a new way to design chips with its Tau Scaling Law.

items.article_content_zh:
台北——中国华为技术公司和一家当地合作伙伴表示，他们已经克服了美国对其使用先进芯片设计工具的限制，该市场长期由美国领导者 Synopsys 和 Cadence 主导，为这家中国科技巨头在国内设计下一代手机和服务器芯片铺平了道路。

鲜为人知的电子设计自动化（EDA）软件提供商Phlexing Technology表示，它一直在与华为合作开发工具包，以根据华为的芯片设计原理（即Tau缩放定律）设计芯片。 Phlexing 董事长何庆表示，战略合作始于 2019 年，致力于开发一套新的 EDA 工具，后来被称为 Tau EDA。

他周二在北京举行的华为创新与知识产权论坛上表示：“华为带来了电信级的严格标准来支持Phlexing的EDA开发。它提升了整个EDA行业。”他补充说，华为正在将Phlexing EDA与其他本土EDA工具供应商联系起来，进行真正的项目工具培训。 “无晶圆厂（芯片制造商）、晶圆厂（芯片厂）和封装厂通过这种机制协同工作。Phlexing EDA 释放了整个链条的巨大生产力，”他说。

华为麒麟芯片架构师刘宇表示，这家中国公司为彻底改革芯片设计流程付出了巨大努力，并克服了许多障碍，以推动该公司自有芯片的东山再起。

“我们必须解决八项主要技术挑战。我们运行了一个涵盖架构、设计、流程工作流程和 EDA 工具的大型项目，”刘说。

这一消息披露之际，华为宣布其专利许可业务收入创历史新高。该公司表示，去年的收入为 8 亿美元，高于 2024 年的 6.3 亿美元，2011 年至 2026 年 9 月期间累计专利许可收入为 69 亿美元。

自从华盛顿于 2019 年 5 月将华为列入所谓的实体清单以来，华为失去了获得美国技术的机会，中国一直致力于减少对外国公司 EDA 的依赖。

2025年，华为的研发支出为1920亿元人民币（290亿美元），占其年收入的21.8%。超过一半的员工（114,000 人）从事研发工作。建有基础技术实验室86个，联合创新实验室180多个。

无线通信占华为活跃授权专利的41%，终端硬件占16%，人工智能和计算占13%。华为目前拥有8000多项人工智能相关专利。

华为首席知识产权官范艾伦告诉记者，该公司已将知识产权部门提升为直接向董事会报告的顶级部门，强调了其对开发专有技术和专利的承诺。此举还反映出领导层致力于加强华为的法律能力，并使知识产权在其战略中发挥更加突出的作用。

世界知识产权组织前总干事弗朗西斯·高锐表示，亚洲已成为全球知识产权领域的主要参与者。

高锐在北京的一个论坛上表示：“所有知识产权申请的 70% 是在亚洲提出的……这反映了亚洲作为技术强国和占世界人口 58% 的市场的卓越地位。”

据华为称，华为的授权合作伙伴包括美国的高通和惠普、欧洲的梅赛德斯-奔驰和大众、以及日本的精工解决方案和三菱扶桑。

华为宣布这一消息之际，正值人工智能行业经历严重波动之际，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌与中国间谍嫌疑人有关系而突然离职，又戏剧性地重新担任首席执行官。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普吹捧了他为确保黄仁勋回归所做的努力，称中国可能挖走他为英伟达的竞争对手华为工作。

items.title: EU officials say the EC is pressing Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX, and XVideos to introduce tougher age checks as it develops a bloc-wide age verification app (Barbara Moens/Financial Times)
items.title_en: EU officials say the EC is pressing Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX, and XVideos to introduce tougher age checks as it develops a bloc-wide age verification app (Barbara Moens/Financial Times)

inline_images.caption: The European Commission is investigating four large adult content sites, including Pornhub, for allegedly breaching the Digital Services Act © Anna Barclay/Gett
inline_images.alt: The European Commission is investigating four large adult content sites, including Pornhub, for alle

items.author: Financial Times
items.article_content:
Four large adult content websites are seeking to reach a deal with the European Commission on preventing children from accessing porn, as the sites try to minimise upcoming fines under the bloc’s push to protect minors online.

The Commission is investigating Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX and XVideos for alleged breaches of the Digital Services Act by failing to adequately protect children from accessing adult content, as minors could access the porn platforms by simply claiming via one click that they are over 18. The DSA — which fully took effect in 2024 and forms part of the bloc’s broader digital rulebook — sets out how tech companies should police the internet.

The probe forms part of a broader European push to protect minors online that also includes a proposal to ban the use of social media, certain gaming platforms and AI chatbots by children under 13.

Since the start of the porn investigation in May last year, the four platforms have submitted co-ordinated commitments to address the concerns, but the Commission found those to be insufficient, two EU officials said.

The Commission is now discussing further remedies with the companies, although they are set to face fines for failing to take adequate measures in the past, the officials said.

Companies that fail to follow the EU digital rules face fines of up to 6 per cent of their global revenue, although the fines are rarely that high. The potential fines were first reported by MLex.

Brussels is simultaneously developing an EU-wide age-verification app that will allow all digital platforms, including porn websites, to confirm the age of a user without revealing additional personal information.

But it will take time to implement that technology, so the Commission is now discussing with the porn sites measures they can take to verify users’ ages in the transition phase. Any such measures would seek to avoid ongoing fines.

“We are looking into what we can accept,” one of the officials said.

The platforms have also raised concerns with the Commission that overly strict checks would lead adults to turn to lesser-known, smaller porn platforms which would be easier to access as they may have less strict age-verification systems.

To avoid this, EU member states have — in parallel with the EU probe — launched a co-ordinated crackdown on smaller platforms under national jurisdictions.

The companies did not immediately reply to a request for comment. The Commission declined to comment.

items.article_content_en:
Four large adult content websites are seeking to reach a deal with the European Commission on preventing children from accessing porn, as the sites try to minimise upcoming fines under the bloc’s push to protect minors online.

The Commission is investigating Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX and XVideos for alleged breaches of the Digital Services Act by failing to adequately protect children from accessing adult content, as minors could access the porn platforms by simply claiming via one click that they are over 18. The DSA — which fully took effect in 2024 and forms part of the bloc’s broader digital rulebook — sets out how tech companies should police the internet.

The probe forms part of a broader European push to protect minors online that also includes a proposal to ban the use of social media, certain gaming platforms and AI chatbots by children under 13.

Since the start of the porn investigation in May last year, the four platforms have submitted co-ordinated commitments to address the concerns, but the Commission found those to be insufficient, two EU officials said.

The Commission is now discussing further remedies with the companies, although they are set to face fines for failing to take adequate measures in the past, the officials said.

Companies that fail to follow the EU digital rules face fines of up to 6 per cent of their global revenue, although the fines are rarely that high. The potential fines were first reported by MLex.

Brussels is simultaneously developing an EU-wide age-verification app that will allow all digital platforms, including porn websites, to confirm the age of a user without revealing additional personal information.

But it will take time to implement that technology, so the Commission is now discussing with the porn sites measures they can take to verify users’ ages in the transition phase. Any such measures would seek to avoid ongoing fines.

“We are looking into what we can accept,” one of the officials said.

The platforms have also raised concerns with the Commission that overly strict checks would lead adults to turn to lesser-known, smaller porn platforms which would be easier to access as they may have less strict age-verification systems.

To avoid this, EU member states have — in parallel with the EU probe — launched a co-ordinated crackdown on smaller platforms under national jurisdictions.

The companies did not immediately reply to a request for comment. The Commission declined to comment.

items.article_content_zh:
四个大型成人内容网站正在寻求与欧盟委员会就防止儿童访问色情内容达成协议，因为在欧盟推动保护未成年人上网的推动下，这些网站试图将即将到来的罚款降到最低。

该委员会正在调查 Pornhub、Stripchat、XNXX 和 XVideos 涉嫌违反《数字服务法》，因为它们未能充分保护儿童访问成人内容，因为未成年人只需一键声称自己已年满 18 岁即可访问色情平台。DSA 于 2024 年全面生效，是欧盟更广泛的数字规则手册的一部分，规定了科技公司应如何监管互联网。

该调查是欧洲保护未成年人在线行动的一部分，其中还包括一项禁止 13 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体、某些游戏平台和人工智能聊天机器人的提案。

两名欧盟官员表示，自去年 5 月开始色情调查以来，四大平台已提交协调承诺来解决这些问题，但欧盟委员会认为这些承诺还不够。

官员们表示，欧盟委员会目前正在与这些公司讨论进一步的补救措施，尽管它们将因过去未能采取适当措施而面临罚款。

不遵守欧盟数字规则的公司将面临高达其全球收入 6% 的罚款，尽管罚款很少这么高。 MLex 最先报道了可能的罚款。

布鲁塞尔正在同时开发一款欧盟范围内的年龄验证应用程序，该应用程序将允许包括色情网站在内的所有数字平台在不透露其他个人信息的情况下确认用户的年龄。

但实施这项技术需要时间，因此委员会现在正在与色情网站讨论在过渡阶段可以采取的措施来验证用户的年龄。任何此类措施都旨在避免持续的罚款。

“我们正在研究我们可以接受什么，”一位官员说。

这些平台还向委员会提出了担忧，认为过于严格的检查会导致成年人转向鲜为人知、规模较小的色情平台，这些平台可能更容易访问，因为它们的年龄验证系统可能不太严格。

为了避免这种情况，欧盟成员国在欧盟调查的同时，对国家管辖范围内的小型平台发起了协调一致的打击行动。

两家公司没有立即回复置评请求。该委员会拒绝发表评论。

items.title: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)
items.title_en: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)

inline_images.caption: The logo of Huawei during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on July 6, 2023. Photo: AFP
inline_images.alt: The logo of Huawei during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on July 6, 2023.

items.author: South China Morning Post
items.article_content:
Huawei Technologies has announced that HarmonyOS, its home-grown, Android-free operating system, has surpassed 100 million installations, marking a milestone in its effort to build a software ecosystem independent of Google’s mobile services amid US-led sanctions.

The Shenzhen-based firm said the total was reached this month across smartphones, tablets and personal computers running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7. Its ecosystem now offered more than 460,000 apps and services from over 12 million registered developers, according to a Huawei statement on Tuesday.

In a social media post on Tuesday, Richard Yu Chengdong, chairman of Huawei’s Consumer Business Group, called the achievement a “landmark moment” and said the ecosystem had crossed a “critical scale threshold”.

“It has officially entered a new phase of maturity, usability and innovation-driven growth,” Yu wrote on China’s social media platform Weibo, which is similar to X.

The milestone comes two years after Huawei debuted HarmonyOS 5 in 2024, its fully self-developed operating system designed to replace Android on the company’s devices. Adoption quickly grew alongside the Chinese tech giant’s strong comeback in the smartphone industry, powered by in-house semiconductors, as the US-sanctioned company stepped up efforts to achieve self-reliance in software and hardware.

In China, HarmonyOS was the second-largest smartphone operating system in the second quarter, accounting for 24 per cent of the market, ahead of the 18 per cent by Apple’s iOS, according to data by Counterpoint Research. Google’s Android still led the market with a 58 per cent share.

Globally, HarmonyOS had only a 5 per cent share in the second quarter, compared with Android’s 75 per cent share and iOS’s 20 per cent, as limited app compatibility continued to limit its reach.

Huawei planned to make a stronger push to expand HarmonyOS internationally, “gradually” bringing the operating system to the global market in the next one to three years, Yu told reporters in September.

Huawei first launched HarmonyOS in China in August 2019, months after Washington added the company to a trade blacklist that blocked access to products using US-origin technologies without explicit approval.

Early similarities in HarmonyOS’s kernel – the core of an operating system that manages how software interfaces with hardware – initially made it compatible with Android apps. But that started to change with HarmonyOS 5, also marketed as HarmonyOS Next.

items.title_zh: 华为鸿蒙系统装机量突破一亿大关
items.summary_zh: 华为宣布鸿蒙系统装机量超1亿，拥有超46万应用服务与1200万注册开发者，生态规模进入成熟期
items.article_content_zh:
华为技术有限公司宣布，其自主研发的、不含 Android 的操作系统 HarmonyOS 的安装量已超过 1 亿，这标志着华为在美国主导的制裁下构建独立于谷歌移动服务的软件生态系统的努力取得了里程碑式的进展。

这家总部位于深圳的公司表示，运行 HarmonyOS 5、6 和 7 的智能手机、平板电脑和个人电脑本月已达到这一目标。根据华为周二的声明，其生态系统目前提供了来自超过 1200 万注册开发者的超过 46 万个应用程序和服务。

华为消费者业务集团董事长余承东在周二的社交媒体帖子中称这一成就是“里程碑式的时刻”，并表示该生态系统已经跨越了“关键规模门槛”。

“它正式进入了成熟、可用性和创新驱动增长的新阶段，”余在中国社交媒体平台微博上写道，该平台与X类似。

这一里程碑是在华为于 2024 年推出 HarmonyOS 5 两年后实现的，这是其完全自主开发的操作系统，旨在取代该公司设备上的 Android。随着这家受到美国制裁的公司加紧努力实现软件和硬件的自力更生，随着这家中国科技巨头在内部半导体的推动下在智能手机行业的强劲复苏，采用率迅速增长。

Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，在中国，鸿蒙操作系统是第二季度第二大智能手机操作系统，占据 24% 的市场份额，领先于苹果 iOS 的 18%。谷歌的Android仍然以58%的份额领先市场。

在全球范围内，HarmonyOS 第二季度的份额仅为 5%，而 Android 的份额为 75%，iOS 为 20%，因为有限的应用程序兼容性继续限制了其覆盖范围。

余承东9月份对记者表示，华为计划加大力度推动HarmonyOS的国际扩张，在未来一到三年内“逐步”将该操作系统推向全球市场。

华为于 2019 年 8 月首次在中国推出 HarmonyOS，几个月前，华盛顿将该公司列入贸易黑名单，禁止未经明确批准使用美国原产技术的产品。

HarmonyOS 内核（管理软件与硬件交互方式的操作系统的核心）的早期相似之处最初使其与 Android 应用程序兼容。但随着 HarmonyOS 5（也以 HarmonyOS Next 的名称进行销售），这种情况开始发生变化。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 华为技术有限公司宣布鸿蒙系统（HarmonyOS）在智能手机、平板及个人电脑端的总装机量已突破1亿台，并拥有超过46万个应用及1200万注册开发者。华为消费者业务集团董事长余承东表示，该系统已跨越关键规模门槛，标志着华为在脱离谷歌移动服务（GMS）后，成功构建起具备商业成熟度与自主可控能力的软件生态系统。

Richard Yu Chengdong, Chairman of the Consumer Business Group, stated that the ecosystem has crossed a critical scale threshold, signaling the system's transition to a mature, self-reliant software platform independent of Google’s mobile services.

The core strategic hurdle remains the transition to HarmonyOS Next to fully decouple from Android legacies while leveraging hardware-software integration to penetrate enterprise and IoT market niches.
