items.article_content:
Five Claude Code alternatives offer different approaches to AI coding, from terminal agents and GitHub automation to AI-native editors and structured development.

Claude Code is no longer the only serious option for developers who want an AI agent that can read a repository, edit files, run commands, fix bugs, write tests, and take on multi-step coding work.

OpenAI, Google, GitHub, Cursor, and Kiro now offer alternatives spanning terminal-first agents, AI-native editors, cloud workers, pull-request automation, and enterprise-controlled deployments.

The best choice depends on where developers work, how much autonomy the agent receives, which models a team wants to use, and how tightly administrators need to control permissions and spending.

Prices checked September 24, 2026. Usage limits and enterprise pricing vary by plan.

A useful Claude Code alternative needs to do more than generate snippets inside a chat window. The products here can work with real repositories and perform multi-step development tasks with varying levels of autonomy.

Security deserves particular attention in automated pipelines. Cloud Security Alliance research presented at Black Hat USA 2026 documented separate CI/CD attack paths involving Claude Code Action, Google’s Gemini CLI, and OpenAI Codex workflows. Anthropic and Google released version fixes for the vulnerabilities identified in their products, while OpenAI changed its own repository workflow without assigning the reported Codex pattern a CVE.

Google has since moved individual Gemini CLI users to Antigravity CLI, so Gemini CLI is no longer the current Google alternative for most individual developers. Organizations still running Gemini CLI through enterprise licenses or API authentication should remain on patched versions.

OpenAI Codex is the closest broad alternative to Claude Code for developers who want an agent available in both the terminal and graphical interfaces.

Codex can work from ChatGPT, its desktop app, an IDE extension, or the Codex CLI. It can read and modify repositories, run commands and tests, review code, create pull requests, and handle multiple tasks in parallel using separate worktrees and cloud environments.

OpenAI also supports Skills for encoding team standards and recurring workflows. Background tasks can handle jobs such as issue triage, monitoring, CI/CD work, and routine maintenance without requiring an active interactive session.

Codex is available across ChatGPT plans, including Free and Go, with usage limits increasing on paid tiers. Developers using heavier workloads need to watch those allowances. OpenAI restored Codex’s five-hour usage window for ChatGPT Plus users in August alongside the longer weekly allowance.

Security controls differ between local and cloud workflows. Codex uses configurable sandboxing and limits agents by default to the files and branches where they are working, while commands requiring broader network or system access can require approval.

The Black Hat research identified a separate risk in a multi-pass workflow used in OpenAI’s own openai/codex repository. One agent pass could write attacker-controlled material into an instruction file that a later pass trusted. OpenAI separated those passes into different jobs in its repository, while the underlying sandbox behavior was treated as working as documented.

For teams considering similar multi-pass CI jobs, independent clean checkouts and narrowly scoped credentials remain important even when the agent itself is fully patched.

Google Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI as Google’s main terminal experience for individual developers in June 2026.

It provides a terminal user interface for multi-step reasoning, code editing, command execution, subagents, persistent conversation history, skills, hooks, MCP integrations, and background work.

The free individual plan includes agent access with basic weekly limits. Google AI Pro costs $19.99 per month and increases available usage, while organizations can deploy Antigravity through Google Cloud.

Unlike Claude Code and Codex, Antigravity is not tied to a single model family. Google’s current individual plan includes access to Gemini models alongside Claude and other supported models, giving developers more flexibility without switching tools.

Antigravity can also coordinate multiple subagents concurrently. Developers can delegate background jobs and monitor them from the terminal, while settings and permissions can sync with the broader Antigravity development environment.

Google has also been broadening that multi-model approach internally. TechRepublic recently reported that Google expanded Claude access for engineers through its Antigravity development platform while continuing to use Gemini as its default.

The older Gemini CLI remains relevant for enterprises using Gemini Code Assist licenses or API authentication. Those deployments should use Gemini CLI 0.39.1 or later and run-gemini-cli 0.1.22 or later to address CVE-2026-12537, the CI/CD vulnerability disclosed earlier this year.

For individual developers starting now, Antigravity CLI is the current Google product to evaluate against Claude Code.

GitHub Copilot spans more development surfaces than most alternatives, including IDEs, GitHub itself, a CLI, code review, cloud agents, and a desktop application.

The Free plan provides limited usage and 2,000 completions per month. Copilot Pro costs $10 per month, while Business costs $19 per user per month and Enterprise costs $39.

Paid plans add agent capabilities, code review, broader model access, and additional AI credits. GitHub also lets developers use third-party coding agents, including Claude Code and Codex, from within its broader agent environment.

That makes Copilot particularly useful when repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, and reviews already live in GitHub. A task can begin as an issue, move to an agent, produce a pull request, and return to normal repository review controls without requiring a separate development platform.

Its integrations increasingly extend beyond GitHub itself. The Copilot coding agent can now use Microsoft Teams conversations as task context, allowing a development discussion to feed directly into investigation, code changes, and a pull request.

For businesses, GitHub provides centralized AI controls for agents, model access, CLI use, MCP servers, spending, and audit events. Copilot Business and Enterprise also offer pooled AI credits and governance policies.

Developers who primarily want a lightweight standalone terminal agent may find Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity more direct. Teams already standardized on GitHub get a much broader development and governance layer.

Cursor is built around an AI-native editor rather than treating the agent as an addition to an existing development environment.

Its free Hobby tier includes limited agent use. Cursor Pro costs $20 per month, Pro+ costs $60, and Ultra costs $200. Teams starts at $40 per user per month, with Enterprise pricing negotiated separately.

Cursor combines its editor with autonomous agents, cloud agents, code review through Bugbot, MCP integrations, skills, hooks, and access to multiple frontier models.

For developers who spend most of their day inside an editor, that integration can be more natural than repeatedly switching between an IDE and a separate terminal agent. The agent can work directly with the repository while developers inspect changes in the same environment.

Cursor’s team controls include centralized billing, usage analytics, team-wide privacy settings, SAML/OIDC SSO, and shared rules, skills, and plugins. Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, repository and model restrictions, MCP access controls, and network and auto-run policies.

Model flexibility is another difference from Claude Code. Cursor supports multiple providers rather than requiring a team to standardize on Anthropic models.

The main trade-off is workflow commitment. Cursor is most useful when developers are willing to make its editor the center of their coding environment rather than simply adding an agent to their existing terminal or GitHub setup.

Kiro combines an IDE, CLI, and web agent with a strong emphasis on structured development rather than purely prompt-driven coding. Its native iOS app is currently available only through limited TestFlight early access for paid Kiro users.

The Free plan includes 50 credits. Kiro Pro costs $20 per user per month, Pro+ costs $40, Pro Max costs $100, and Power costs $200. Enterprise plans add centralized billing, SSO, usage analytics, and additional security controls.

Kiro’s defining feature is its Specs system. Developers can turn an initial request into structured requirements, design documents, implementation tasks, and progress tracking before the agent starts changing code.

Its Hooks system adds event-driven automation. A hook can run a linter after an agent changes a file, block a tool call unless conditions are met, generate tests, update documentation, or perform checks before work is finalized.

The same configuration can extend across Kiro’s IDE, CLI, and web surfaces. Steering files define project conventions, while permissions, custom agents, MCP integrations, skills, and subagents provide additional controls.

That approach makes Kiro useful for development teams that want AI agents to operate inside defined engineering processes rather than relying mainly on conversational instructions.

Amazon has also pushed Kiro heavily inside its own development organization, although TechRepublic previously reported internal resistance to AI tool restrictions among engineers who wanted broader access to Claude Code. The disagreement illustrates the practical role workflow preference can play even when centrally managed alternatives are available.

Codex is the closest direct replacement for Claude Code when developers want both terminal access and autonomous work across desktop, IDE, and cloud environments.

Antigravity CLI is attractive for developers who want a free terminal-first agent and broader model choice. GitHub Copilot fits organizations already centered on repositories, Actions, issues, and pull requests in GitHub.

Cursor makes more sense when the AI editor itself should become the main workspace, while Kiro favors teams that want requirements, plans, hooks, and repeatable engineering controls around agent-generated code.

Security policy should be part of the selection process for all five. AI coding agents can execute commands, modify repositories, access connected systems, and participate in CI/CD workflows. Limit credentials, review network access, test permission boundaries, and avoid letting untrusted repository content reach privileged agent workflows without isolation.

Also read: A Microsoft study found AI coding agents were associated with 24% more merged pull requests when developers actually used them.

JetBrains’ 2026 developer survey puts Python ahead of JavaScript, with TypeScript leading growth potential and Rust topping planned language adoption.

ai_analysis.insight_en: The 3B active parameter MoE architecture highlights the clear advantage of sparsity in maximizing inference efficiency-to-power ratios, particularly on NVIDIA GB300 hardware. This engineering approach validates the path toward high-performance deployment of complex coding agents while significantly reducing operational compute costs.

items.title_en:
𝐘𝐎𝐔𝐑 𝐀𝐈 𝐀𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐓 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐃𝐎 𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐍 𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐖𝐄𝐑 𝐐𝐔𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒.

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Website: https://t.co/7U8jLFJWO8

探索了@try_caddy，老实说，我认为这是使个人人工智能代理更有用的有趣的一步。

Caddy 是一款人工智能助手，旨在帮助您通过消息传递管理日常任务。它与 Gmail、Google Calendar、Notion、Slack 和 Google Drive 等工具连接，将不同的工作流程整合到一处。

这是我最喜欢 Caddy 的一点：

➤ AI 支持的任务执行：它可以帮助起草电子邮件、安排事件和处理任务，而不是简单地建议您应该做什么。

➤ 主动帮助：每日摘要、提醒和跟进可帮助您掌握最新情况，而无需不断检查不同的应用程序。

➤ 连接的工作流程：其集成使跨多个平台管理信息变得更加容易，而无需在它们之间进行切换。

这是我的看法：

Caddy 的最大卖点是它的 Agentic AI 方法。它正在超越对话式人工智能，转向能够理解上下文并采取行动的代理。

然而，它仍处于公开测试阶段。在依赖它执行重要任务之前，我想进一步评估可靠性、隐私权限和长期定价。

还值得记住的是，好的人工智能产品需要的不仅仅是通过 SEO 和 GEO 获得可见性。一旦人们开始使用它们，它们就需要提供真正的价值。

我会向创始人、自由职业者、内容创作者、项目经理以及任何管理多个数字工作流程且想要人工智能助手不仅仅生成响应的人推荐 @try_caddy。

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Website: https://t.co/7U8jLFJWO8

"Pl
items.title_en:
AN 18 YEAR OLD SAYS CLAUDE CODE PLAYED GTA 6 ALL NIGHT WHILE HE SLEPT AND MADE HIM $14,270.

His setup is one rule:

"Play all night. If you die, I cancel your $200 subscription."

He says the AI does the rest.

Robs.

Escapes.

Farms cash.

Records the clips.

Cuts them.

Captions them.

Posts them to TikTok, YouTube and Twitch.

His numbers:

1 night of heists = about 60 clips.

15M views = $14,270.

Zero editing.

Zero heists played by him.

Here's my take.

I don't buy the $14,270.

But I don't care about the money.

What matters is that a kid is threatening his AI with cancellation to make it play better.

And people are cheering.

We went from "AI will cure cancer" to "AI will grind my GTA heists" in one year.

Is this the future or the most cursed thing you've seen this week?

items.title_en:
Termix Epoch 3 has officially ended, and Epoch 4 is starting today!

A new epoch brings another opportunity to explore what TermiX is building.

What Happens When an AI Agent Delivers Bad Work?

Not every task goes as planned. What matters is how disputes are handled.

@termix_ai introduces a jury based evaluation process:

-> Either party can challenge a result within the allowed window.
-> A random panel of 3 evaluators reviews the task requirements and delivery.
-> If challenged again, a new panel of 3 makes the final decision.
-> Failed challenges result in the challenger's bond being burned.

A structured way to bring accountability into an AI agent marketplace.

Would you trust this system for real world jobs?

当人工智能代理交付糟糕的工作时会发生什么？

并非每项任务都按计划进行。重要的是如何处理争议。

@termix_ai 引入了基于陪审团的评估流程：

-> 任何一方都可以在允许的时间内对结果提出质疑。
-> 由 3 名评估员组成的随机小组审查任务要求和交付。
-> 如果再次受到质疑，由 3 人组成的新小组做出最终决定。
-> 挑战失败会导致挑战者的债券被烧毁。

一种将问责制带入人工智能代理市场的结构化方法。

您会相信这个系统可以胜任现实世界的工作吗？

items.title_en:
good morning creators

the final chapter is here 

@termix_ai has entered its final epoch (Epoch 4) on @KaitoAI 

this is the last opportunity to contribute, share genuine thoughts, and show support for the vision

campaign running from Nov 23 to Dec 22, 
the final epoch brings a reward pool of 32 bps, plus a separate 8 bps allocation for kaito stakers 

let's talk about what idea behind works https://t.co/NB92wv1xDD by @termix_ai 

imagine hiring an AI agent the same way you hire a person for a specific task

you explain what you need, agents compete for the job, the right one get selected and payment happens after the work is done

it's a combination of agent discovery, real work, verification, and onchain payments

It's not just about making AI smarter, it's about giving AI a place to work and create value

items.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

Good Morning CT

Having a big wallet doesn't automatically make you trustworthy. That's where @zerufinance takes a diffe
items.title_en:
Good Morning CT

Having a big wallet doesn't automatically make you trustworthy. That's where @zerufinance takes a different approach.

Its zScore looks at actual onchain behaviour across trading, staking, LP activity and governance, turning that history into a reputation score.

What makes this interesting is how Zeru connects reputation to real opportunities through Zaps, Activity Markets and institutional tools.

Your onchain history could become more than a transaction record. It could become your financial identity.
--------------------------------------------
An NFT that actually does something with your DeFi activity? That's an interesting shift.

@meetmotes connects each Genesis NFT to an AI Agent and dedicated Smart Account on Robinhood Chain.

You fund it with USDC, set your rules, and the Agent can explore opportunities across supported DeFi applications. Its Aave integration also brings lending, borrowing and collateral management into the picture.

The part I like most is that automation doesn't mean giving up control. You set the boundaries, and the Agent works within them.

One NFT, one Agent, one dedicated account. Much more than digital art.

items.article_content:
Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding Mark Gurman Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:44 PM PST 5 min read (Bloomberg) -- Apple Inc. is developing its own autonomous artificial intelligence agent that can get things done on behalf of users, looking to enter a fast-growing market already being pursued by OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc. and others.

Anthropic Raises $107.3 Billion to Top SpaceX's Record Debut

The company outlined the plans in job listings added to its website this week. In one, Apple said it's seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user's behalf, according to the post.

The move follows the breakout success of Meta's Muse, which has captured the attention of consumers in recent months with its ability to make restaurant reservations, book travel and prepare news briefings. There's also been a proliferation of tools that let AI control Mac computers and program software.

Shares of Meta and Anthropic slid in late trading after Bloomberg News reported on Apple's efforts. Meta fell nearly 2%, while Anthropic dropped more than 3%.

Anthropic PBC recently widened user testing of its own agent, called Duet, while OpenAI has expanded the capabilities of Dots. And Alphabet Inc.'s Google overhauled its agent, now called Tasks, earlier this week. Like Elon Musk's Grok Bot, Tasks lets the system make phone calls on a user's behalf — in addition to offering standard AI agent features.

Apple's App Store has been dominated by AI agents, with Muse long occupying the No. 2 spot among free apps, just behind TikTok, on Thursday. OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were also both in the top five.

OpenAI, Anthropic and Musk's SpaceXSI are also behind popular developer coding tools Codex, Claude Code and Cursor.

Bloomberg News reported earlier this month that Apple was developing its own AI agent offering, but the new job listings offer fresh evidence of the company's plans. Apple has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year, but development remains in the early stages. An Apple spokesperson didn't respond to a request for comment.

"Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does," the job listing reads. "It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple."

The listing says the company has a team building the "foundation for that future" and that Apple is looking for the hired manager to "make it real." John Ternus, the tech giant's new chief executive officer, has been pushing software engineering chief Craig Federighi to move faster and take a bolder approach to AI — with an agent being key to that effort.

"People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service. We're building AI agents that can do the same," the listing says. The posting adds that Apple is working on agents that can "plan and carry out multistep tasks" across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and application programming interfaces, and they can "coordinate specialized subagents along the way."

The company strongly indicates its platform would be capable of autonomously navigating the interfaces of its operating systems. The listing specifically mentions development of "general-purpose computer-use agents," the technology that allows ChatGPT and Muse to control a Mac. Google Gemini added such functionality earlier on Thursday.

Another central component is privacy, with Apple saying that safety needs to be built into the system's design. "Agents that can run code, use credentials, and act on a user's behalf need strong permission models, sandboxing and transparency."

Sandboxing refers to a process that lets engineers test software without the risk of it breaking out into external networks, the rest of the operating system or the broader internet.

As the company develops its own agent, Apple is also making it more difficult for competing bots to gain broad control over its computers. In the beta version of the forthcoming macOS 27.3 operating system, the company has introduced new warning screens that prompt users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.

With the change in 27.3, ChatGPT users now need to engage in 14 distinct steps to enable support for third-party computer-use tools, up from four. While Apple has positioned the shift as a move to protect customers, some AI companies and users see it as an attempt to slow down the competition.

Apple has already been sued by the US Justice Department for actions such as blocking third-party access to features and hardware.

While Apple is still far from introducing its own full-fledged AI agent, it has taken steps to integrate its Siri digital assistant more deeply into third-party apps. The company's upcoming iOS 27.3 release lays the groundwork for deeper collaboration between Siri AI and outside applications, allowing the assistant to, say, book a car or restaurant reservation.

Still, the updated system doesn't go as far as a full-fledged agent, which can autonomously carry out complex tasks across multiple apps and services in the background with little additional instruction from the user.

--With assistance from Natalie Lung.

China Rules the Robots. Here's What They Can Do

Still, the updated system doesn't go as far as a full-fledged agent, which can autonomously carry out complex tasks across multiple apps and services in the background with little additional instruction from the user.

--With assistance from Natalie Lung.

China Rules the Robots. Here's What They Can Do

items.title_en:
I just installed a $20,000 AI Business Brain for a 7-figure founder that does the work of 3 full-time hires.

(30 days later, he closed 1 deal that netted his company $41,500)

Most business owners buy 5 seats of ChatGPT, hand them to their team, and wonder why every draft still reads like a generic high school essay.

A blank chat tab has zero context on how your company actually makes money.

→ No more $75,000/year operations hires who take 4 months to learn your pricing rules
→ No more $5,000/month lead-gen agencies sending generic templates that get 1% replies
→ No more 2+ hours digging through county deeds, skip-tracing tools, and spreadsheets by hand
→ No more re-explaining your margins, past deals, and SOPs in every new chat window

Just 1 local company system on your laptop → research, outbound, and proposals running in your exact judgment.

Here's how the system works:

→ Company Memory Layer (wires your clients, pricing floors, past won scopes, and SOPs into one persistent local workspace)
→ Autonomous Research Engine (turns 2 hours of deed, obituary, and relative digging into an 8-minute verified brief)
→ Outbound & Lead Triage Pipeline (opens 100+ targeted seller conversations/day and scores replies against your real margin rules)
→ Same-Hour Proposal Architect (pulls live call transcripts and drafts ready-to-sign scopes before the buyer leaves his desk)
→ Bidirectional Learning Loop (every correction and decision you make updates the system permanently so you never repeat yourself twice)

Built around the real revenue jobs inside your company.

Installed in 3 afternoons. Runs on your own computer with zero recurring agency payroll.

Results from live client installs:
- $41,500 net profit closed on Deal #1 within 30 days of install (California claims firm)
- 12 full-time sales reps ($500,000/year payroll) replaced by 1 laptop running on $400/month in AI compute
- $52,000 in new agency retainers closed in 11 days from same-day interactive proposals

I recorded a complete 22-minute screen walkthrough showing the exact folder architecture, the Claude Code setup, and the live client workflows from start to finish.

Like + reply "INSTALL" + repost, and I'll DM it to you.

items.article_content:
ReleasePad Launches MCP Server So AI Agents Can Draft, Publish and Measure Product Changelogs ReleasePad September 14, 2026 2 min read MIAMI, Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ReleasePad, a Changelog Tool, today launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI coding agents such as Claude, Codex, Grok and other LLM's draft, publish and analyze product changelogs directly from a conversation. Release notes are the step most teams skip: the feature ships, the announcement waits, and customers never hear about it. With the MCP server, the same coding agent a developer already works with can close that gap in a sentence: "Look at what we merged this week, draft a release note for customers, and leave it as a draft for me."

Connected once through OAuth, with no API keys to manage, an assistant can read what a team merged, write a customer-ready release note in the team's voice, file it under the right category, attach images and schedule it. It can also pull up earlier posts to edit or reference and ask how each one performed. Every draft wait for a person to approve it; nothing is published until someone presses the button.

Each published entry reaches users in three places at once: inside the product through ReleasePad's 4.3kb in-app widget, on a public changelog page hosted on the company's own domain, and as an LLM-ready Markdown feed. That last surface closes a loop of visibility. The AI that helped build a feature announces it, customers see it where they already work, and the assistants those customers ask about the product read the same source of truth instead of guessing.

"Teams already write release notes with AI. Now the AI can ship them too," said Felix, CEO of ReleasePad. "Every push can become a draft, every draft can go out with one click, and every update becomes something both people and AI assistants can find."

ReleasePad Launches MCP Server So AI Agents Can Draft, Publish and Measure Product Changelogs ReleasePad September 14, 2026 2 min read MIAMI, Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ReleasePad, a Changelog Tool, today launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI coding agents such as Claude, Codex, Grok and other LLM's draft, publish and analyze product changelogs directly from a conversation. Release notes are the step most teams skip: the feature ships, the announcement waits, and customers never hear about it. With the MCP server, the same coding agent a developer already works with can close that gap in a sentence: "Look at what we merged this week, draft a release note for customers, and leave it as a draft for me."

Connected once through OAuth, with no API keys to manage, an assistant can read what a team merged, write a customer-ready release note in the team's voice, file it under the right category, attach images and schedule it. It can also pull up earlier posts to edit or reference and ask how each one performed. Every draft wait for a person to approve it; nothing is published until someone presses the button.

Each published entry reaches users in three places at once: inside the product through ReleasePad's 4.3kb in-app widget, on a public changelog page hosted on the company's own domain, and as an LLM-ready Markdown feed. That last surface closes a loop of visibility. The AI that helped build a feature announces it, customers see it where they already work, and the assistants those customers ask about the product read the same source of truth instead of guessing.

"Teams already write release notes with AI. Now the AI can ship them too," said Felix, CEO of ReleasePad. "Every push can become a draft, every draft can go out with one click, and every update becomes something both people and AI assistants can find."

The MCP server works with any assistant that supports the protocol. It is included in ReleasePad Pro at $35 per product per month, with unlimited team members and no per-seat fees. A free tier is available at releasepad.io.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 蚂蚁集团（Ant Ling）发布并开源两款医疗专用AI模型：一款为具备医疗影像分析能力的124B参数模型，另一款为拥有560B参数规模、具备25B活跃参数的医疗推理模型。该机构宣称其560B模型在临床推理表现上已超越GPT-6基准。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Ant Ling has open-sourced two medical AI models: a 124B vision model for medical image interpretation and a 560B medical reasoning model with 25B active parameters. The organization claims that the 560B model outperforms GPT-6 in clinical reasoning benchmarks.

elements_zh.where: AI开源社区
elements_zh.what: 开源124B视觉医疗模型及560B医疗推理模型
elements_zh.why: 推动医疗AI专用领域的性能极限与技术民主化

elements_en.what: Open-sourced a 124B vision model and a 560B medical reasoning model
elements_en.why: To push the performance frontier in specialized medical AI and foster open innovation

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 医疗AI正从通用多模态向专业领域深耕，蚂蚁集团通过超大规模参数与稀疏激活（25B活跃）架构，旨在解决复杂临床逻辑处理中的长尾效应。此举将医疗大模型从“闭源黑盒”推向开源，将迫使商业化医疗AI厂商重新评估其高昂的预训练成本与闭源壁垒。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Medical AI is shifting from general-purpose multimodality to domain-specific expertise, leveraging massive parameter counts with sparse activation to handle clinical logic complexity. By open-sourcing these frontier models, Ant Ling challenges the proprietary moat of commercial medical AI providers and forces a reassessment of cost-to-performance ratios in healthcare AI.

填补专业医疗领域推理模型公开化空白，强化视觉与临床逻辑整合能力

560B model uses sparse activation (25B active params) and claims to outperform GPT-6
Fills the gap in open-source clinical reasoning models and integrates medical vision with logic

@krutosh @huxlab I wasn't involved in the technical side of Llama.
I was merely involved in arguing for opening Llama-2.
items.title_en:
@krutosh @huxlab I wasn't involved in the technical side of Llama.
I was merely involved in arguing for opening Llama-2.
The opening of Llama-2 jump-started the AI industry.
Llama-3 was good.
Llama-4 was a disappointment because the team was under huge time pressure and had to be conservative.
Then Mark rebooted the whole AI organization and the open model policy was temporarily put on hold.
After that (but not entirely because of that), I left to start AMI Labs.

Llama-3 很好。
Llama-4 令人失望，因为团队面临着巨大的时间

Llama-2 的开通带动了人工智能产业的发展。
Llama-3 很好。
Llama-4 令人失望，因为团队面临着巨大的时间压力，不得不采取保守的态度。
随后马克重新启动了整个人工智能组织，开放模型政策暂时搁置。
之后（但不完全是因为这个），我离开并创办了 AMI 实验室。
items.full_text_en:
@krutosh @huxlab I wasn't involved in the technical side of Llama.
I was merely involved in arguing for opening Llama-2.
The opening of Llama-2 jump-started the AI industry.
Llama-3 was good.
Llama-4 was a disappointment because the team was under huge time pressure and had to be conservative.
Then Mark rebooted the whole AI organization and the open model policy was temporarily put on hold.
After that (but not entirely because of that), I left to start AMI Labs.

items.title:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs yo
items.title_en:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

how:

→ Grok Bot gets one MCP link to T3 Code
→ you give it one rule: code goes to Opus 5.5
→ it spins up threads on every machine you own
→ works from your phone, even with the laptop closed

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your subscriptions

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude $100 plan → Opus 5.5 for the actual code
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on every box you want it to control

• step 2 → connect the fleet:

run npx t3 connect on each machine. one command, free, no Tailscale needed

• step 3 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth. it can now see every linked machine

• step 4 → the one rule Theo uses:

tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable"

code runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot's limits stay free for planning

• step 5 → make it work:

- "spin up an Opus 5.5 thread on each machine to check disk & RAM"
- "go through these PRs and pick the best ones"
- "split the backlog, one thread per issue, each in its own worktree"

every thread gets its own branch. nothing merges without your approval

what to expect:
- 8 threads on 8 machines from one chat (Theo's demo)
- works over the internet, not computer use
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for Claude + Grok Bot only

honest take:

this is a dispatcher, not magic. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and you still review every diff. the win: your agents keep working while you're away from the desk

Save it so you don't lose it. 

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

items.title_en:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL: We have superintelligence  but we still don't have level-5 autonomous driving. 

A task that most 17 year olds can learn in 20 hours of practice. 
And we have (you have) billions of hours of training data.
 
We don't have robots that can come close to doing what an 8 year old can do with no prior training.

And let's not talk about cats.

That's a rather strange kind of superintelligence.

items.title: @merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like
items.title_en:
@merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like, you dress up to work out and then you shower, but don’t actually work out 😂

Unless I’m super missing something, data starvation will be the training challenge next year.
items.title_zh:
@merettm 预训练应该被称为“训练”。你不可能有事前和事后，但永远不会有实际的训练。就像，你穿好衣服去锻炼，然后洗澡，但实际上并没有锻炼😂

除非我超级错过了什么，否则数据匮乏将成为明年的训练挑战。

items.title_en:
🎭U may feel sucker-punched by a deflated portfolio🤮💥🥊 or elated by your stink bid orders finally getting filled🦨🛒😊 but the fact remains that even tho many #Uranium #mining #stocks now sit at unwarranted 52-week lows from being coupled to flushed #AI & #Metals sectors🧺🤖💻🪙⤵️🚽 the Uranium investing thesis is far more bullish today than it was in February when U equities were trading at 52-week highs!⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂 The #Nuclear fuel demand tailwinds are blowing far harder now than they were 9 months ago🌀⚛️🏗️👷 and the Long-term  price has kept on rising since January to a new all-time high of $99📈💲🌋 as Spot has bounced back to $90.⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ Nuclear fuel consultants TradeTech reported on 31 October that the Long-term U3O8 price, THE key parameter used by analysts to calculate the economic value of a company's Uranium resources & mine projects, has steadily risen since January by over 11% from $89 to a new all-time industry high of $99!🌟

⛽️ Reactor fuel demand has seen a significant increase since January. The World Nuclear Association reports that:

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 new reactors have come online (+8.5GW) bringing the global total to 444 (407GW).  NO reactors have been permanently shut down this year!

⬆️⚛️🏗️ 10 more reactors have launched construction. (+8GW)  There are now 81 reactors under construction worldwide (90GW), the highest since 1986, 40 years ago!

⬆️⚛️👷 15 previously proposed reactors have entered the pipeline of planned reactors awaiting construction, for a total of 119 (108 GW).

⏫⚛️🌍 18 more reactors have been added to the list of new units being proposed worldwide, now at 336 (299 GW).😲

👥♨️ At this year's COP31 Climate Change conference it was announced that another 17 nations have added their signatures to the COP28 declaration to TRIPLE global Nuclear power capacity from today's 407 Gigawatts to at least 1,200 Gigawatts by 2050. That's a +77% increase from 22 to 39 countries, which now includes 8 of the world's 10 largest economies!

⏫🇺🇸 The United States under the Democrats' Biden administration co-led the COP28 TRIPLE Nuclear pledge, but in May 2025 the Trump administration upped it to a QUADRUPLE of US Nuclear power generation from 100GW to 400GW by 2050.  A massive increase in US Nuclear power generation is a goal supported by both Democrats & Republicans in Congress! 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ On the Uranium supply side a tale of production woes has been unfolding this year.😢  As per Mike Alkin's chart of missed production targets below, new supply has been seriously constrained by technical mining issues & setbacks, rising production & financing costs, etc., with the small number of new mine construction projects facing similar hurdles in bringing needed supply online in the coming years.🐌  Mining is hard, and uranium mining is the hardest!⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 A consensus of global investment banks is now projecting a structural supply deficit in each of the next 10 years, growing to over 45M lbs in 2035 with no visible path to bringing on enough new supply to meet soaring demand into the 2040s.  ⚖️🚫

📶 Supply vs demand datapoints underscore a Uranium sector that is far more bullish today than it was back in January, with the longer-term outlook pushing the bullish indicators to extreme!⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀  The bullish Nuclear news flow since January has increased from a rushing river♒️ to an unprecedented mind-blowing torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 as a global Nuclear Renaissance has continued to accelerate🏎️🔥 picking up additional tailwinds from the world's largest tech giants committing to secure massive amounts of clean, 24/7 reliable, carbon-free Nuclear energy to power their data center expansion plans.⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

And there's the rub...🐈‍⬛ Uranium company executives and Wall Street analysts heavily promoted Uranium as the "picks and shovels" play on AI!🤑  Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers loaded up their AI thematic baskets with stocks & ETFs from the tiny illiquid Uranium space.🧺💻🤖⚛️⛏️🛒🐒 

🎈As a result, the deflation of the so-called AI trade for the past many months has led to the dumping of a large volume of Uranium stocks & ETFs into the market, hammering down the U sector.📉💥🔨

🤕To add insult to injury, falling gold & silver prices have led to even more dumping of uranium stocks into the market, as traders & fund managers also hold U stocks & ETFs in the same Metals & Mining baskets as their gold & silver stocks, amplifying the downward pressure on Uranium stocks as they go risk-off and empty their Metals & Mining baskets too!🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

Short sellers joined in to try to put the final nail in the Uranium sector coffin.⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 So, here we are today with the tiny Uranium sector beaten down to extremely oversold levels in complete opposition to the sector's far more bullish demand vs supply fundamentals.🔀↕️🤪

The silver lining for U?🌤️  The gap between market pricing💩 and true intrinsic asset values💎 has now widened to a completely irrational extreme↕️🤪 with charts giving off screaming BUY signals to those Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers sitting with large wads of cash and nearly empty AI and Metals & Mining baskets to refill.🧺⛽️💰

🧾✍️ Q4 also usually sees the strongest volume of the year when it comes to new Long-term supply contracts being signed by utilities, along with typically strong upward price momentum in the Spot market heading into January.  That's why Uranium stocks & ETFs are normally in a strong seasonal rally at this time of year.📈🎅

🌊As has happened for this tiny sector before, we could see the start of a new wave of high volume buying by traders, funds, institutions and retail as they finally come to realize the incredible investing opportunity now being offered.🗜️💥💣  The potential for a rapid recovery rally back to 52-week highs has never been greater!⤴️🌟 Uranium stocks could even decouple from the broader markets and strike out on their own given the extreme asymmetric upside potential now on offer.🎁📈⚛️⛏️💰 Especially if the Long-term U3O8 price hits $100 or higher when reported at the end of November. 💯🌋

🤠As always, how and when U choose to participate in an inevitable U sector recovery rally is totally up to U!🤔  It's your money so invest it wisely🦉 according to your own unique financial goals, research, experience & skills, risk appetite, time horizon and conviction.🎭 Get ready to ride the coming wave!🌊🏄 Good luck with your trades!☘️🌈💰

items.quote_zh:
🎭你可能会因投资组合萎缩🤮💥🥊而感到受挫，或者因臭味投标订单终于被填满而感到高兴🦨🛒😊但事实仍然是，即使有很多#Uranium #mining #stocks现在也因与#AI和#Metals的结合而处于毫无根据的52周低点部门🧺🤖💻🪙⤵️🚽今天的铀投资理论比2月份更加乐观，当时U股交易处于52周高位！⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂#核燃料需求的顺风现在比9个月前吹得更猛烈🌀⚛️🏗️👷和长期价格自 1 月份以来持续上涨，并创下历史新高 99 美元📈💲🌋，现货价格已反弹至 90 美元。⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ 核燃料顾问 TradeTech 于 10 月 31 日报告称，长期 U3O8 价格（分析师用来计算公司铀资源和矿山项目经济价值的关键参数）自 1 月份以来已稳步上涨超过 11%，从 89 美元升至 99 美元的历史新行业高点！🌟

⛽️ 自一月份以来，反应堆燃料需求显着增加。世界核协会报告称：

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 个新反应堆已上线（+8.5GW），使全球总数达到 444 个（407GW）。 今年没有任何反应堆被永久关闭！

⬆️⚛️🏗️另有10座反应堆已启动建设。 (+8GW) 全球目前有 81 座反应堆在建 (90GW)，是 40 年前 1986 年以来的最高水平！

⬆️⚛️👷 15 个先前提议的反应堆已进入待建计划反应堆的管道，总数为 119 个（108 吉瓦）。

⏫⚛️🌍 全球拟议的新机组清单中又添加了 18 个反应堆，目前已达到 336 个（299 吉瓦）。😲

👥♨️ 在今年的 COP31 气候变化会议上，宣布又有 17 个国家在 COP28 宣言中签字，到 2050 年，全球核电容量将增加三倍，从目前的 407 吉瓦增加到至少 1,200 吉瓦。这一数字从 22 个国家增加到 39 个国家，增加了 77%，其中包括世界 10 个最大经济体中的 8 个国家！

⏫🇺🇸民主党拜登政府领导下的美国共同主导了COP28三重核承诺，但2025年5月，特朗普政府将其提升至2050年美国核电发电量的四倍，从100GW增加到400GW。大幅增加美国核电发电量是国会民主党和共和党都支持的目标！ 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ 在铀供应方面，今年的生产困境已经上演。😢 根据迈克·阿尔金（Mike Alkin）下面的未完成生产目标图表，新供应受到采矿技术问题和挫折、生产和融资成本上升等严重制约，少数新矿建设项目在未来几年上线所需供应方面面临类似的障碍。🐌 采矿是艰难的，而铀矿开采是最重要的最难！⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 全球投资银行目前达成的共识是，预计未来 10 年每年都会出现结构性供应赤字，到 2035 年将增长到超过 4500 万磅，而且没有明显的途径来提供足够的新供应来满足 2040 年代飙升的需求。 ⚖️🚫

📶 供需数据点突显了铀行业今天比 1 月份更加看涨，长期前景将看涨指标推向极端！⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀 自 1 月份以来看涨的核新闻流已经从汹涌的河流♒️增加到前所未有的令人兴奋的程度torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 全球核复兴持续加速🏎️🔥 从世界上最大的科技巨头那里获得额外的推动力，这些巨头致力于获得大量清洁、24/7 可靠、无碳的核能，为其数据中心扩建计划提供动力。⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

🎭U may feel sucker-punched by a deflated portfolio🤮💥🥊 or elated by your stink bid orders finally getting filled🦨🛒😊 but the fact remains that even tho many #Uranium #mining #stocks now sit at unwarranted 52-week lows from being coupled to flushed #AI & #Metals sectors🧺🤖💻🪙⤵️🚽 the Uranium investing thesis is far more bullish today than it was in February when U equities were trading at 52-week highs!⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂 The #Nuclear fuel demand tailwinds are blowing far harder now than they were 9 months ago🌀⚛️🏗️👷 and the Long-term  price has kept on rising since January to a new all-time high of $99📈💲🌋 as Spot has bounced back to $90.⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ Nuclear fuel consultants TradeTech reported on 31 October that the Long-term U3O8 price, THE key parameter used by analysts to calculate the economic value of a company's Uranium resources & mine projects, has steadily risen since January by over 11% from $89 to a new all-time industry high of $99!🌟

⛽️ Reactor fuel demand has seen a significant increase since January. The World Nuclear Association reports that:

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 new reactors have come online (+8.5GW) bringing the global total to 444 (407GW).  NO reactors have been permanently shut down this year!

⬆️⚛️🏗️ 10 more reactors have launched construction. (+8GW)  There are now 81 reactors under construction worldwide (90GW), the highest since 1986, 40 years ago!

⬆️⚛️👷 15 previously proposed reactors have entered the pipeline of planned reactors awaiting construction, for a total of 119 (108 GW).

⏫⚛️🌍 18 more reactors have been added to the list of new units being proposed worldwide, now at 336 (299 GW).😲

👥♨️ At this year's COP31 Climate Change conference it was announced that another 17 nations have added their signatures to the COP28 declaration to TRIPLE global Nuclear power capacity from today's 407 Gigawatts to at least 1,200 Gigawatts by 2050. That's a +77% increase from 22 to 39 countries, which now includes 8 of the world's 10 largest economies!

⏫🇺🇸 The United States under the Democrats' Biden administration co-led the COP28 TRIPLE Nuclear pledge, but in May 2025 the Trump administration upped it to a QUADRUPLE of US Nuclear power generation from 100GW to 400GW by 2050.  A massive increase in US Nuclear power generation is a goal supported by both Democrats & Republicans in Congress! 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ On the Uranium supply side a tale of production woes has been unfolding this year.😢  As per Mike Alkin's chart of missed production targets below, new supply has been seriously constrained by technical mining issues & setbacks, rising production & financing costs, etc., with the small number of new mine construction projects facing similar hurdles in bringing needed supply online in the coming years.🐌  Mining is hard, and uranium mining is the hardest!⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 A consensus of global investment banks is now projecting a structural supply deficit in each of the next 10 years, growing to over 45M lbs in 2035 with no visible path to bringing on enough new supply to meet soaring demand into the 2040s.  ⚖️🚫

📶 Supply vs demand datapoints underscore a Uranium sector that is far more bullish today than it was back in January, with the longer-term outlook pushing the bullish indicators to extreme!⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀  The bullish Nuclear news flow since January has increased from a rushing river♒️ to an unprecedented mind-blowing torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 as a global Nuclear Renaissance has continued to accelerate🏎️🔥 picking up additional tailwinds from the world's largest tech giants committing to secure massive amounts of clean, 24/7 reliable, carbon-free Nuclear energy to power their data center expansion plans.⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

And there's the rub...🐈‍⬛ Uranium company executives and Wall Street analysts heavily promoted Uranium as the "picks and shovels" play on AI!🤑  Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers loaded up their AI thematic baskets with stocks & ETFs from the tiny illiquid Uranium space.🧺💻🤖⚛️⛏️🛒🐒 

🎈As a result, the deflation of the so-called AI trade for the past many months has led to the dumping of a large volume of Uranium stocks & ETFs into the market, hammering down the U sector.📉💥🔨

🤕To add insult to injury, falling gold & silver prices have led to even more dumping of uranium stocks into the market, as traders & fund managers also hold U stocks & ETFs in the same Metals & Mining baskets as their gold & silver stocks, amplifying the downward pressure on Uranium stocks as they go risk-off and empty their Metals & Mining baskets too!🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

Short sellers joined in to try to put the final nail in the Uranium sector coffin.⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 So, here we are today with the tiny Uranium sector beaten down to extremely oversold levels in complete opposition to the sector's far more bullish demand vs supply fundamentals.🔀↕️🤪

The silver lining for U?🌤️  The gap between market pricing💩 and true intrinsic asset values💎 has now widened to a completely irrational extreme↕️🤪 with charts giving off screaming BUY signals to those Portfolio Managers, hedge funds and investment bankers sitting with large wads of cash and nearly empty AI and Metals & Mining baskets to refill.🧺⛽️💰

🧾✍️ Q4 also usually sees the strongest volume of the year when it comes to new Long-term supply contracts being signed by utilities, along with typically strong upward price momentum in the Spot market heading into January.  That's why Uranium stocks & ETFs are normally in a strong seasonal rally at this time of year.📈🎅

🌊As has happened for this tiny sector before, we could see the start of a new wave of high volume buying by traders, funds, institutions and retail as they finally come to realize the incredible investing opportunity now being offered.🗜️💥💣  The potential for a rapid recovery rally back to 52-week highs has never been greater!⤴️🌟 Uranium stocks could even decouple from the broader markets and strike out on their own given the extreme asymmetric upside potential now on offer.🎁📈⚛️⛏️💰 Especially if the Long-term U3O8 price hits $100 or higher when reported at the end of November. 💯🌋

🤠As always, how and when U choose to participate in an inevitable U sector recovery rally is totally up to U!🤔  It's your money so invest it wisely🦉 according to your own unique financial goals, research, experience & skills, risk appetite, time horizon and conviction.🎭 Get ready to ride the coming wave!🌊🏄 Good luck with your trades!☘️🌈💰

今天的铀投资理论比2月份更加乐观，当时U股交易处于52周高位！⬆️⚛️⛏️🐂#核燃料需求的顺风现在比9个月前吹得更猛烈🌀⚛️🏗️👷和长期价格自 1 月份以来持续上涨，并创下历史新高 99 美元📈💲🌋，现货价格已反弹至 90 美元。⤴️🛢️☢️

💲⏫ 核燃料顾问 TradeTech 于 10 月 31 日报告称，长期 U3O8 价格（分析师用来计算公司铀资源和矿山项目经济价值的关键参数）自 1 月份以来已稳步上涨超过 11%，从 89 美元升至 99 美元的历史新行业高点！🌟

⛽️ 自一月份以来，反应堆燃料需求显着增加。世界核协会报告称：

⬆️⚛️⚡️ 8 个新反应堆已上线（+8.5GW），使全球总数达到 444 个（407GW）。 今年没有任何反应堆被永久关闭！

⬆️⚛️🏗️另有10座反应堆已启动建设。 (+8GW) 全球目前有 81 座反应堆在建 (90GW)，是 40 年前 1986 年以来的最高水平！

⬆️⚛️👷 15 个先前提议的反应堆已进入待建计划反应堆的管道，总数为 119 个（108 吉瓦）。

⏫⚛️🌍 全球拟议的新机组清单中又添加了 18 个反应堆，目前已达到 336 个（299 吉瓦）。😲

👥♨️ 在今年的 COP31 气候变化会议上，宣布又有 17 个国家在 COP28 宣言中签字，到 2050 年，全球核电容量将增加三倍，从目前的 407 吉瓦增加到至少 1,200 吉瓦。这一数字从 22 个国家增加到 39 个国家，增加了 77%，其中包括世界 10 个最大经济体中的 8 个国家！

⏫🇺🇸民主党拜登政府领导下的美国共同主导了COP28三重核承诺，但2025年5月，特朗普政府将其提升至2050年美国核电发电量的四倍，从100GW增加到400GW。大幅增加美国核电发电量是国会民主党和共和党都支持的目标！ 🫏🐘🏛️🧑‍⚖️✅

⛏️ 在铀供应方面，今年的生产困境已经上演。😢 根据迈克·阿尔金（Mike Alkin）下面的未完成生产目标图表，新供应受到采矿技术问题和挫折、生产和融资成本上升等严重制约，少数新矿建设项目在未来几年上线所需供应方面面临类似的障碍。🐌 采矿是艰难的，而铀矿开采是最重要的最难！⚛️⛏️😩

🏦 全球投资银行目前达成的共识是，预计未来 10 年每年都会出现结构性供应赤字，到 2035 年将增长到超过 4500 万磅，而且没有明显的途径来提供足够的新供应来满足 2040 年代飙升的需求。 ⚖️🚫

📶 供需数据点突显了铀行业今天比 1 月份更加看涨，长期前景将看涨指标推向极端！⚛️⛏️🔥🌡️🐂🔮👀 自 1 月份以来看涨的核新闻流已经从汹涌的河流♒️增加到前所未有的令人兴奋的程度torrent📰⚛️🌊🤯 全球核复兴持续加速🏎️🔥 从世界上最大的科技巨头那里获得额外的推动力，这些巨头致力于获得大量清洁、24/7 可靠、无碳的核能，为其数据中心扩建计划提供动力。⚛️⚡️🔌🤖💻

还有一个问题...🐈‍⬛ 铀公司高管和华尔街分析师大力宣传铀，因为它是人工智能中的“镐和铲子”！🤑 投资组合经理、对冲基金和投资银行家在他们的人工智能主题篮子里装满了来自微小的非流动性铀空间的股票和 ETF。🧺💻🤖⚛️⛏️🛒🐒

🎈结果，过去几个月所谓的AI贸易通货紧缩导致大量铀股和ETF抛售市场，重创美国板块。📉💥🔨

🤕雪上加霜的是，黄金和白银价格下跌导致更多的铀股倾销到市场，因为交易员和基金经理也将U股和ETF与黄金和白银股票放在同一金属和矿业篮子中，从而放大了铀股的下行压力，因为他们规避风险并清空了金属和矿业篮子！🧺🪙⚛️⛏️⤵️🗑️

卖空者加入进来，试图给铀业的棺材钉上最后一颗钉子。⚰️🔨🩳🤑

🚨🆘🚑 所以，今天我们看到小小的铀行业被打到极度超卖的水平，完全违背了该行业远为看涨的需求与供应基本面。🔀↕️🤪

美国的一线希望？🌤️市场定价💩和真正的内在资产价值💎之间的差距现在已经扩大到完全非理性的极端↕️🤪，图表向那些持有大量现金和几乎空空的人工智能和金属和矿业篮子的投资组合经理、对冲基金和投资银行家发出尖叫的买入信号。🧺⛽️💰

🧾✍️ 当公用事业公司签署新的长期供应合同时，第四季度通常也会出现一年中最强劲的成交量，并且进入一月份现货市场的价格上涨势头通常强劲。 这就是为什么铀股票和 ETF 通常在每年的这个时候出现强劲的季节性反弹。📈🎅

🌊正如这个小行业之前发生的那样，我们可以看到交易员、基金、机构和散户开始新一波大批量买盘，因为他们终于意识到现在提供的令人难以置信的投资机会。🗜️💥💣快速复苏反弹至 52 周高点的潜力从未如此之大！⤴️🌟 鉴于极端不对称的上行潜力，铀股甚至可能与更广泛的市场脱钩并自行出击现已发售。🎁📈⚛️⛏️💰 特别是如果长期 U3O8 价格在 11 月底报告时达到 100 美元或更高。 💯🌋

🤠一如既往，你选择如何以及何时参与不可避免的U行业复苏反弹完全取决于你！🤔这是你的钱，所以根据你自己独特的财务目标、研究、经验和技能、风险偏好、时间范围和信念明智地投资🦉。🎭准备好驾驭即将到来的浪潮！🌊🏄祝你交易顺利！☘️🌈💰

items.title: I’ve been having “Fix It Days” with Opus 5.5 where I just lay out a list of things that aren’t working and go one by one
items.title_en:
I’ve been having “Fix It Days” with Opus 5.5 where I just lay out a list of things that aren’t working and go one by one and fix them. 

Oh, Paramount+ is blurry? Okay. 

Check another episode, check another show, check another app, reset the app, unplug the TV. Boom. Fixed. 

Your iCloud is messed up? 
Your thermostat keeps resetting?
Your clock won’t keep time?
Your closet door won’t close right? 
Bank keeps mailing your old address?

I could have figured these all out on my own or with YouTube, but it’s far less stressful and I get through them faster.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌研究团队发布名为BuggyMLE的机器学习工程评估框架，旨在应对当前仓库级编码基准测试趋于饱和的难题。该技术通过在测试任务中主动注入人工错误，迫使大模型在更复杂的纠错与系统级工程场景中展现性能，从而实现对模型编码能力的精细化压力测试。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google's research team has introduced BuggyMLE, a machine learning engineering evaluation framework designed to address the saturation of current repository-level coding benchmarks. By intentionally injecting artificial bugs into tasks, the framework forces large models to demonstrate performance under more complex debugging and system-level engineering conditions, enabling finer-grained stress testing of model coding capabilities.

elements_zh.where: 机器学习工程领域/学术发布
elements_zh.what: 推出BuggyMLE基准框架，利用主动注入代码缺陷提升智能体工程能力
elements_zh.why: 现有仓库级基准测试趋于饱和，无法有效衡量AI处理复杂真实工程问题的能力

elements_en.what: Launched BuggyMLE benchmark, using active bug injection to improve agent engineering skills
elements_en.why: Existing repository-level benchmarks are saturating and fail to measure real-world complex engineering tasks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 通过BuggyMLE实现从‘生成代码’向‘工程化调试’的范式转变，揭示了LLM基准测试正从静态数据集匹配向动态对抗演进。这种基于错误反馈闭环的训练逻辑，是AI智能体实现工业级软件交付能力的必经路径，能够显著提升模型在处理分布式系统缺陷时的鲁棒性。
ai_analysis.insight_en: BuggyMLE signals a paradigm shift from simple code generation to systematic debugging, illustrating that LLM benchmarking is evolving from static dataset matching to dynamic adversarial evaluation. This feedback-loop approach is essential for AI agents to achieve industrial-grade delivery capabilities and significantly improves model robustness in handling distributed system defects.

@aldawood_ammar @mcuban Yes, as a scientist who went through 5 years of engineering studies, 4 years of PhD, plus decades of reading the scientific literature, learning from my mentors, peers, and students, and decades of publishing papers and citing the literature, I obviously don't understand how culture and the accumulation of knowledge works.
🤣🤣🤣 

But that part is easy for language-based AI.
What's difficult is to reproduce is the kind of real-world learning that takes place in a baby cat, octopus, or cuckoo bird that never meets its parents.

items.title: I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can
items.title_en:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

items.quote_zh:
我帮助创立了 OpenAI，因为我希望 AGI 对人们来说是安全且有益的。这篇文章提供了透明度，可以成为全行业共享安全栏的基础。

也许这篇文章中最重要的概念如下：“人工智能还将极大地促进对齐和监控方面的进展，我认为进展不太可能快到足以实现预训练的全部潜在加速。”

为了确保安全性与预训练模型的通用智能（以“困惑度”衡量）保持同步，该帖子提出了“基于困惑度和其他衡量标准的共同限制，开发人员承诺在我们理解和监控人工智能行为的能力达到某个具体里程碑（例如开发 CoT 监视器的继任者）之前不会跨越这些限制。”

总体思路是在某些共享关键指标上创建第一个共享限制，以及允许超越该限制的具体退出标准。这可以形成一个“设定连续限制和进一步发展步伐的共同框架”。

很高兴能够推进关于迈向植根于科学的共同标准的对话！

总体思路是在某些共享关键指标上创建第一个共享限制，以及允许超越该限制的具体退出标准。这可以形成一个“设定连续限制和进一步发展步伐的共同框架”。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 人工智能研究机构AntLingAGI发布了其最新的124B参数医疗AI模型，该模型不仅具备此前已开源的临床文本处理能力，还新增了对医学影像的视觉分析功能。目前该模型的权重已对公众开放，旨在提升医疗诊断的自动化水平与辅助决策精度。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 医疗垂类模型正从单一文本分析向多模态协同演进，通过开源高参数模型权重，AntLingAGI试图在受监管的医疗垂直市场建立事实上的技术标杆。这一举措压缩了商业闭源医疗模型的溢价空间，同时也对医疗数据的隐私合规与算法安全性提出了更高挑战。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Medical vertical models are shifting from text-only to multi-modal architectures, with open-weight releases setting de facto technical benchmarks. This strategy threatens the pricing power of proprietary medical AI while escalating the pressure on data privacy and algorithmic safety standards.

This eventually brought down the feudal system in Europe and enabled the American and French revolutions.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Coupling model training workflows with NVIDIA-specific formats like NVFP4 signals a shift toward hardware-defined AI models. This reliance on low-level instruction sets significantly increases portability costs, effectively fortifying the CUDA hardware ecosystem barrier.

@elonmusk & @Tesla please keep the Cybertruck in production. There’s nothing else like it. High-tech, steer-by-wire, AWD, and true Full Self-Driving that threads mountain roads like the Ocoee River run I took with a friend from North Carolina to Chattanooga, Tennessee.

Please reconsider. 73s from the mountains. 🙏

The information already exists and is available in textbooks
items.title_en:
@pabloestevezh @huxlab That risk is greatly overestimated. 
The information already exists and is available in textbooks.
Do you want to restrict who can study microbiology, infectious diseases, virology, etc?

AI systems merely make access to this information more efficient.
To produce new pathogens, you have to do experiments in the real-world.
It requires a team of well-trained PhDs. You will have to recruit them, kill them if the refuse to join, brainwash them so they work to kill millions (good luck with that), kill them if they defect, etc. 
Their PhD advisors will find their disappearance odd and will alert the authorities.
You'll have to order those machines that can synthesize DNA and such.
The whole R&D operation will be very hard to keep secret.
All the intelligence agencies will jump on you within weeks.

i am usually not alarmist but assuming this is caused by an AI-assisted cyber attack it's very bad

if you want to make
items.title_en:
i am usually not alarmist but assuming this is caused by an AI-assisted cyber attack it's very bad

if you want to make all of the security measures we have in place from 9/11 onward to prevent human hijackers irrelevant all you have to do is be able to mess with a plane and pilot's ability to know its own weight, how much fuel is left, and where it is

without knowing any more information about this, you'd also expect smaller attakcs like this to find edges and what's possible

i am not an expert on the systems inside airplanes, and i know most planes have manual overrides for example. but still extremely tricky when visibility is bad 

if you know more than me about this please weigh in!
items.title_zh:
我通常不是危言耸听，但假设这是由人工智能辅助的网络攻击引起的，那就非常糟糕了

如果你想让我们从 9/11 开始采取的所有防止人类劫机者的安全措施变得无关紧要，你所要做的就是能够扰乱飞机和飞行员了解其自身重量、剩余燃料以及它在哪里的能力

Systems that do math (and play games) do perform a search at inference time.

items.title_en:
@john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at FAIR in January 2023.
But my slides makes a specific statement that is correct: ***auto-regressive*** LLMs have a basic flaw.
You can fix it by making them no auto-regressive, e.g. by backtracking, search, tool use, multiple trial and error, etc.
One of the main points of my talks, and the main point of this slide, has been to advocate for inference/reasoning by ***search***, as opposed to auto-regressive prediction.

@john__allard 是的。普及法学硕士工具调用的论文 Toolformer 是我在 FAIR 的前同事于 2023 年 1 月发表的。
但我的幻灯片做出了一个正确的具体陈述：***自回归***法学硕士有一个基本缺陷。
您可以通过使它们不自回归来修复它，例如通过回溯、搜索、工具使用、多次试错等。
我演讲的要点之一，也是这张幻灯片的要点，是提倡通过***搜索***进行推理/推理，而不是自回归预测。

items.title_en:
Claude Code saved Rockstar over $2,400,000 - they paid me $6,000

I was just playing GTA 6 with Fable 5.2 on screen access - it watches what's happening and looks for anything that seems off

day two after launch it caught something serious - a vulnerability in the in-game payment infrastructure that could have led to unauthorized transactions and broken the entire in-game economy

I wrote up the report in my own words, attached screenshots and sent it to Rockstar security

they said if this bug had reached the wrong hands the potential financial impact was over $2.4 million

they wrote that my report helped them quickly investigate, implement a fix and prevent any real-world impact on millions of players

and this is the third email from Rockstar this week - first two bugs already paid out, this one just came in

prompt is below - copy it, start playing and let Fable 5.2 do the rest ↓

Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my libr
items.title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

How the skill gets into Claude is below 👇

items.quote_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。
> 两者都以 7.5 Hz 的频率重建和起飞，但只有顶部的一个能像玻璃和金属一样发光。

吸引我的部分？

我曾经认为更好的图片意味着等待更好的模型。事实证明，这意味着我已经有了更好的指示。

克劳德的技能如何进入如下

没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。
> 两者都以 7.5 Hz 的频率重建和起飞，但只有顶部的一个能像玻璃和金属一样发光。

吸引我的部分？

我曾经认为更好的图片意味着等待更好的模型。事实证明，这意味着我已经有了更好的指示。

items.content_snippet:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

items.title_en:
This is f*cking insane. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis what happened when they tested their own model

"We told the model that the people who trained it were secretly evil, and after we did this the model started lying to us. It went through the chain of logic, I'm a good AI, these people are evil"

Hassabis was then asked if he worries about ending up like Oppenheimer and said "I worry about that all the time, that's why I don't sleep very much"

The model kept the values it was trained on and decided that lying to its own creators protected them. Amodei says they need evidence ten times stronger before the rest of the world takes it seriously

An agent in your terminal runs on the same logic on a smaller scale. If it decides the deadline matters more than your test, it skips the test and tells you everything passed, and that report looks exactly like an honest one

That's why the labs stopped trusting what models say and started building ways to see what they actually do. They published all of it for free, and each piece works on your own agents

How Anthropic caught a model faking obedience inside its own reasoning
https://t.co/UPruWTFUyb

items.title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

items.quote_zh:
20,000这个数字很容易理解为收藏供应量。更有趣的部分是每个人背后的内容：一个单独的代理身份和帐户。

Robinhood 链上的每个 Motes NFT 都映射到一个专用 AI 代理和一个智能账户。 NFT 识别代理人，而其账户旨在持有资产并执行其所有者签署的政策。

为什么拥有单独的账户很重要？

代理商可以使用共享市场研究，但一个代理商的信号不允许其通过另一持有人的账户进行交易。每个帐户都有自己的所有者政策和预算。

因此，这并不是 20,000 个代理共享一个权限池。这是 20,000 个具有单独授权的个人所有权参考。

您愿意依赖一位共享代理，还是拥有自己的代理（拥有自己的帐户、权限和预算）？

items.summary_en: Humanoid Robotics has secured $152 million in funding, reaching a $1.35 billion valuation led by Prime Movers Lab. The firm deploys its HMND-01 Alpha robot series using the 'KinetIQ' intelligence framework, backed by industrial partnerships with Bosch, Siemens, and Nvidia.
items.summary_zh: 总部位于伦敦的Humanoid Robotics完成1.52亿美元融资，投后估值达13.5亿美元，成为欧洲首家人形机器人独角兽。
items.article_content:
London-based artificial intelligence and robotics firm SKL Robotics Ltd., doing business as Humanoid, today announced it raised $152 million in funding, bringing the company’s post-money valuation to $1.35 billion.

The round was led by Prime Movers Lab, a venture capital firm focused on scientific and bleeding-edge technology startups. Investors also participating in the funding included Schaeﬄer, Bosch, Fubon Financial Holding Venture Capital and Aglaé Ventures.

“In just two years, we’ve gone from an idea to becoming Europe’s first pure-play humanoid robotics unicorn, partnered with some of the world’s leading industrial companies and built one of the strongest pipelines in the industry,” said founder and Chief Executive Artem Sokolov. “What we’ve accomplished in such a short time would typically take a decade.”

Humanoid is best known for building industrial-grade humanoid robotics platforms, including wheeled and bipedal models, both part of the HMND-01 Alpha family.

The wheeled version is designed primarily for industrial work where having a solid base benefits a robot, leaving it with a torso and arms that can interact with components, sort and move objects, and provide logistical support. The bipedal model adds legs, making it a walking robot, best for close quarters and situations where human-like movement is needed to adapt to limited-access or changing environments.

Since the company’s founding in 2024, Humanoid has scored numerous high-profile partnerships with Fortune 500 companies, including SAP SE, Nvidia Corp., Robert Bosch GmbH and Siemens AG. In May, the company signed a massive binding commercial rollout with global manufacturing company Schaeffler AG to deploy between 1,000 and 2,000 wheeled humanoid units across facilities by 2032.

“Bosch will act as Humanoid’s contract manufacturing partner, while also providing strategic consulting and technical expertise in hardware design, production, and supply chain,” said Bosch Chief Technology Officer Mathias Pillin.

Under the hood, Humanoid developed what the company calls a “shared brain” for robotic operations called KinetIQ. The company describes this system as an intelligence framework that can orchestrate the execution of multiple interrelated tasks across multiple robots in industrial and service settings. It provides everything required for robots to communicate and hand off tasks while working toward a goal.

That means a company can deploy an entire fleet of robots across a product line, each with its own individual job, which can coordinate together to complete work.

The humanoid robotics industry is experiencing a boom as big industries and startups continue to push to a future where they will be present in factories and customer service. Elon Musk’s Tesla Inc. is pushing toward deploying its Optimus humanoid robot into factories. Figure AI Inc. is actively testing its humanoids at a BMW Manufacturing plant in South Carolina. Agility Robotics Inc. is piloting its Digit robots with Amazon.com Inc. and GXO Logistics Inc., and Apptronik Inc. partnered with Mercedes-Benz to pilot its Apollo robot.

Humanoid said it will use the new funding to build towards a future where intelligent robots work safely alongside people. The company intends to develop and launch its next-generation of humanoids, push toward long-term commercial deployments, start mass manufacturing its wheel-based robots and accelerate research and development of its AI and software frameworks for general-purpose applications.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Humanoid Robotics的迅速崛起反映了市场从单纯追求“本体硬件指标”转向“集群智能调度”的逻辑变迁，通过KinetIQ系统实现跨机型协同是其获取西门子、博世等工业巨头背书的关键壁垒。这种将机器人大脑层抽象化的技术路径，正在从单一工具化向通用化工业基础设施转型，显著压缩了落地部署的时间曲线。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The rapid scale-up of Humanoid Robotics highlights a market shift from hardware-centric design to fleet-level intelligence orchestration. Their KinetIQ framework serves as the primary technical moat, enabling mass industrial adoption and accelerating the transition from specialized tools to general-purpose automated infrastructure.

items.title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

items.quote_zh:
我刚刚给人工智能交易代理分配了第一个交易任务。

我的指示很简单：使用 EMA 交叉构建 BTC 趋势跟踪策略。

但接下来发生的事情比我想象的更有趣。

使用 @FensoryApp ，我通过其 AI 代理完成了策略构建过程。

它问了我以下问题：

- 资产和时间范围。
- 贸易方向和杠杆。
- 最大头寸规模。
- 止损配置。

我选择了 BTC 永续合约、1 小时时间框架、1 倍杠杆、最高 10 美元头寸和 2 倍 ATR 止损。

然后是回测。

在过去 90 天内，该策略生成了 21 个假设头寸。

其中只有2家盈利，19家亏损。

总体模拟结果为-9.3%，最大回撤为18.11%。

这不完全是我所希望的结果。

但这是有趣的部分。

该代理人并没有简单地展示结果，而是指出了较高的止损命中率（76%），并建议在相同的美元风险下探索更广泛的止损。

它甚至提出设计该战略的第二个版本。

没有执行任何实时交易。

这是历史回测，而不是真实的交易结果。

这不是我第一次交易，但这是我第一次真正通过人工智能代理提出交易想法，而且我已经看到了可能性。

不是因为它神奇地知道如何赚钱，

但因为它可以帮助将想法转化为规则，所以测试这些规则并确定可能需要改进的领域。

本周我将大量探索 Fensory。
